Johnny and his mum had been walking across the grass for a few minutes when Johnny noticed something strange.

"Mummy, why did that man and that lady separate?" he asked, pointing at two people walking away from each other.

"Well, Johnny," his mum said, "Sometimes people decide that it is better for them to be separate. It is sad, but it happens."

Johnny was quiet for a few moments. He listened to the silence around him, the silence of the birds and the trees. Then he said, "But why can't they talk? I don't want them to be deaf."

His mum gave Johnny a hug. "No, Johnny, that's not what I mean. When I talk about people separating, I mean separating their lives. They can still talk, but sometimes it is just better for them to no longer be together."

Johnny nodded, understanding a little better. He smiled and said, "It's okay, Mum. They don't have to be deaf to be separate." His mum smiled back, proud of her son's understanding.

The person said, "I want to bow to the tree and give thanks for this beautiful day."

But soon, they hear a loud noise. It is dad. He is home from work. He comes into the garage and sees the mess. He is not happy. He says they have to clean up. He says they have to be nice and share the track. He says they have to be careful with the power.

Tom and Lily feel sorry. They say they are sorry. They help dad clean up. They put the cars and the track back in the box. They hug dad and mom. They say they love them. "I'm sorry, Ben," Lily said. "I should have listened to you."

"That's okay, my sweeties," Mommy said. "I love you more than any cake. And I have another mug. Let's make the cake together."

He wanted to have it. He picked it up and looked at it closely. He forgot what his mom said and touched the car.

Sam saw a yellow plane that was brighter and louder than his blue plane. He wanted to have it. He picked it up and pressed a button. He forgot what his mom said and touched the plane.

The store owner saw Ben and Sam touching the toys. He was angry. He shouted at them and told them to put the toys back. He said they were not allowed to touch the toys. He said they were bad boys. He scared Ben and Sam.

Ben and Sam felt very sorry. They put the toys back and ran to their mom. They told her what happened and apologized. Their mom hugged them and said it was okay. She said they made a mistake, but they learned from it. She said they should always listen to what she says and respect other people's things. She said they were good boys.

Ben and Sam nodded and said they understood. They thanked their mom and said they loved her. They said they loved their own toys too. They said they did not need new toys. They said their brown car and blue plane had spirit. They said they would polish them and play with them happily.

Anna was a spoiled girl who always wanted more toys. She had a big room full of dolls, cars, books and games, but she was never happy. She always frownd when her mommy and daddy said no to her.

One day, Anna saw a new toy on TV. It was a shiny rocket that could fly in the air and make noises. Anna wanted it very much. She ran to her mommy and said, "Mommy, mommy, I want the rocket! Please buy it for me!"

Mommy shook her head and said, "No, Anna, you have enough toys already. You don't need the rocket. It is too expensive and too dangerous. Why don't you play with what you have?"

Anna was very angry. She threw a tantrum and said, "I hate you, mommy! You are mean and bad! I want the rocket! I want the rocket!"

Mommy was very sad. She said, "Anna, you are being very rude and ungrateful. You should be thankful for what you have. There are many children in the world who have no toys at all. They have no food, no water, no home. They live in poor lands where there is war and sickness. They would be happy with just one doll or one car. You should think about them and be kind and generous."

Anna did not listen. She kept screaming and crying. She ran to her room and slammed the door. She did not care about other children. She only cared about herself.

The next day, Anna woke up and saw a big box on her bed. She thought it was the rocket. She was very excited. She opened the box and saw a note from mommy. It said, "Dear Anna, I have a surprise for you. I have donated all your toys to a charity that helps children in need. They will send them to a faraway land where they will make many children happy. I hope you will learn to share and appreciate what you have. Love, mommy."

Anna was shocked. She looked inside the box and saw nothing. All her toys were gone. She had nothing left. She felt a big pain in her heart. She realized how selfish and spoiled she had been. She wished she could have her toys back. She wished she could say sorry to mommy. She wished she could be a good girl.

She ran to mommy and hugged her. She said, "Mommy, mommy, I'm sorry. I was wrong. I was spoiled. I don't need the rocket. I don't need any toys. I only need you. Please forgive me. Please love me."

Mommy smiled and kissed her. She said, "I forgive you, Anna. I love you. You are my precious girl. I'm proud of you. You have learned a valuable lesson. You have learned to be thankful and compassionate. You have learned to be happy with what you have."

Anna smiled and said, "Thank you, mommy. I love you too. You are the best mommy in the world. You have given me the best gift ever. You have given me your love."

"That is lightning, Ben. It is a big spark of electricity that comes from the clouds when they are angry," Mom explained.

"Why are the clouds angry, Mom?" Mia asked, curious.

"Well, sometimes the clouds get too full of water and they need to let it out. They make rain and thunder and lightning to do that. It is their way of talking to each other," Mom said.

"Wow, that is amazing, Mom. Can we talk to the clouds too?" Ben wondered.

"Maybe, but we have to be careful. Lightning can be dangerous if it hits something or someone. We have to stay inside when there is lightning and wait until it stops," Mom said.

They went inside with Mom and enjoyed their snack and their book. They were not afraid of the lightning anymore. They were curious and happy.

"Sure, Tom, here you go," Mom says and gives him more sauce.

Mia does not like sauce. She thinks it is too red and rough. She only eats a little pasta and pushes her plate away.

"Mia, why don't you eat your sauce? It is good for you," Mom says.

"I don't like sauce, Mom. It is rough and hurts my tongue," Mia says.

"Mia, sauce is not rough. It is smooth and yummy. Try a little bit, please," Mom says.

Mia shakes her head. She does not want to try sauce.

Tom sees Mia's sauce. He wants more sauce.

"Please, Mia, can I have your sauce?" Tom says.

Mia looks at Tom. She does not like sauce, but she does not want to share either.

"No, Tom, it is my sauce. You have your own sauce," Mia says.

Tom and Mia start to argue. They both want Mia's sauce.

Mom hears them and sighs. She has an idea.

"Tom, Mia, stop fighting. I have a surprise for you. Do you want to see it?" Mom says.

Tom and Mia stop arguing. They like surprises.

"Yes, Mom, what is it?" they say.

Mom smiles and brings out a big cake. It has chocolate and cream and sprinkles.

"Wow, Mom, a cake!" Tom and Mia say.

"Yes, a cake. For dessert. But you have to finish your lunch first. And share your sauce," Mom says.

Tom and Mia look at the cake. It looks so good. They look at their sauce. It does not look so bad.

"Okay, Mom, we will finish our lunch and share our sauce," they say.

Mom is happy. She cuts the cake and gives them each a slice.

Tom and Mia eat their pasta and sauce. They share and say please and thank you. They eat their cake and smile. They like cake a lot. They hug Mom and say they love her.

Mom hugs them back and says she loves them too. She is proud of them. They are good kids.

Ben and Mia liked to play in the attic. They found many old things there, like books, hats, and toys. But there was one thing they never touched: a big, dark chest in the corner. Their mom told them it was scary and they should stay away from it.

One day, when mom was busy, Ben and Mia went to the attic again. They played with the books and the hats and the toys. But Ben was curious. He wanted to see what was in the chest. He said to Mia, "Let's open it. Maybe there are more toys inside."

Mia shook her head. She remembered what mom said. She said, "No, Ben. It's scary. Mom said so. We should not open it."

But Ben did not listen. He walked to the chest and tried to lift the lid. It was heavy and dusty. He pulled hard and hard. He made a loud noise. He opened the chest.

Mia screamed. Out of the chest came a big, black spider. It had many legs and eyes. It looked angry. It jumped on Ben and bit him. Ben cried and cried. He dropped the lid and ran to Mia. They hugged each other and ran out of the attic.

Mom heard the noise and the screams. She ran to the attic and saw the spider. She was scared too. She grabbed a broom and hit the spider. She threw it out of the window. She hugged Ben and Mia and said, "I'm sorry, my loves. Are you okay? I told you not to open the chest. It was an old store for spiders. They are very scary and dangerous. You should never touch it again."

Ben and Mia nodded. They said, "We're sorry, mom. We won't touch it again. We love you, mom."

Mom smiled and said, "I love you too, my loves. Come on, let's go downstairs and have some cookies. And don't worry, the spider is gone. It won't come back."

As they walked around the store, Lily saw her friend Tommy. She ran up to him and said, "Hi Tommy! How are you?" Tommy replied, "I'm good, thanks. What are you doing here?" Lily said, "I'm helping my mommy with the grocery shopping. We need to talk to each other later, okay?" Tommy nodded and said, "Sure, see you later!" 

After they finished shopping, Lily and her mommy went home and put away all the groceries. Lily was so happy to have helped her mommy and to have seen her friend at the grocery store. From that day on, she always loved going to the grocery store with her mommy.

Her mom thought for a moment and said, "Well, Lily, ladybugs are not really pets. They like to live outside and fly around. They need fresh air and food and water. But can I nap with it first?" she asked.

Her mom laughed and said, "Sure, Lily. You can nap with it first. But be careful not to squish it or lose it. And don't forget to put the lid on the jar." she said. Lily hugged her mom and said, "Thank you, mom. You are the best." She took the jar and went to her room. She put the jar on her bed and lay down next to it. She watched the ladybug crawl on the glass and said, "Hello, ladybug. You are my friend. Thank you for coming to see me. I hope you have a good day too." She closed her eyes and fell asleep. The ladybug rested on the lid and waited for Lily to wake up. It was happy to meet Lily, but it also wanted to go back to the flowers. It hoped that Lily would let it go soon. It was a good and lucky and pink beetle.

Tom did not want to stay on the sea. He wanted to go back to the land. He said to Polly, "Please, Polly, let's go back. I don't like fun like this. I like fun when the sun is shining and the sea is calm."

But Polly did not listen to Tom. She said to Tom, "You are a sailor, Tom. You have to be brave. You have to take the storm. It is not so bad. Look, the cloud is getting smaller and the wind is getting softer. See, the storm is going away."

Tom looked at the sky and the sea. He saw that Polly was right. The storm was going away. The sun was coming out and the sea was getting calm. Tom felt better. He said to Polly, "You are right, Polly. The storm is going away. Maybe it was not so scary after all. Maybe it was a little fun. Thank you, Polly, for being my friend."

Polly smiled and said to Tom, "You are welcome, Tom. You are my friend too. And you are a good sailor. You took the storm. You were brave. Now let's sail some more and have more fun."

Her mom said, "That's right. You are a smart girl. But don't forget to shake the crumbs off the toast before you put it on the plate. Otherwise, they will make a mess on the table."

Lily said, "OK, mom. I will shake the toast." She put two slices of bread in the toaster and pushed the lever down. She watched the toaster with excitement. She liked the sound and the smell of the toast.

She brought the plate to the table and said, "Mom, I made toast for you and me. Do you like it?"

The moral value of the story is: Kindness is a good quality that makes others happy.

Their mom heard them and came to the pool. She saw them fighting and scolded them.

"Stop it, both of you! Why are you fighting over a toy? You should share and play nicely, not be selfish and mean. How would you feel if someone took your toy and wouldn't let you play with it?" she said, taking the shark from them.

Tom and Lily felt ashamed and sorry. They realized they were wrong, and they apologized to each other.

"I'm sorry, Tom. I shouldn't have tried to take the shark from you. Can we share and play together?" Lily said, hugging Tom.

"I'm sorry, Lily. I shouldn't have kept the shark from you. Of course we can share and play together. You're my sister and I love you." Tom said, hugging Lily back.

They gave the shark to their mom and asked her to put it back in the pool. Then they picked up their water guns and sprayed each other again, laughing and having fun.

They learned that sharing is caring, and that fighting is not fun. They were happy to be pirates and sharks, and to be friends.

Bob was sad because his favorite place to play was spoiled. But Max felt bad and wanted to help. Together, they cleaned the fountain until it was sparkling again. Now, Bob and Max play together at the fountain every day, and they became the best of friends.

Polly told Timmy that she needed help to find her lost toy. Timmy and Polly looked all around the purple tree. They looked up, they looked down, and they looked in the middle. Finally, they found the toy under a big leaf. They were very happy and played together for the rest of the day.

Once upon a time, there was a big pot. The pot was very selfish. It did not like to share. One day, a little boy named Tim came to the pot. Tim was hungry and wanted some food.

"Please, Mr. Pot, may I have some food?" Tim asked. The selfish pot did not want to share, but it did not want Tim to be sad. So, the pot slapped its side and out came a small piece of bread for Tim. Tim was happy and said, "Thank you, Mr. Pot!"

The next day, a little girl named Sue came to the pot. Sue was hungry too. She asked the pot, "Can I have some food, Mr. Pot?" The pot thought about how it had shared with Tim the day before, and decided to share with Sue too. It slapped its side again, and out came a small piece of bread for Sue. Sue was happy and thanked the pot.

From that day on, the pot learned that sharing was good. It was not selfish anymore. It slapped its side every day to give food to all the hungry children. And everyone was happy.

Lily's mom told the man that it was okay and that he should surrender to the police so he could make things right. The man thanked her and left the shop. Lily asked her mom why the man was sad, and her mom explained that sometimes people make mistakes but it's important to try and make things right.

Timmy watched as the steam rose up from the pot. He was fascinated by it. 

"Can we eat the steam?" Timmy asked.

"No, we can't eat steam. But we can eat what's inside the pot once it's done cooking," his mom explained.

Timmy waited patiently as his mom cooked dinner. When it was ready, they sat down to eat together. Timmy enjoyed his meal and was happy to learn something new about steam.

Finally the dog lifted the lid. Inside it found a big, juicy bone! It was happy and started to gobble it down.

The rain had stopped and the dog was no longer wet. It had a full tummy and a happy heart.

Three year old Lucy was feeling very worried. She asked her mom, "What's a pilot?"

Her mom smiled and answered, "A pilot is a special kind of person who flies airplanes. They take people on trips and take them to new places."

Lucy was still a bit worried, so she asked her mom, "What if the pilot gets lost?"

Her mom laughed and answered, "Don't worry. Pilots are very smart and they have special tools to help them find their way. They are always careful and know exactly where they are going."

Lucy nodded and smiled. She was so happy when she got answers to all her questions!

One day, a gifted octopus wanted to test itself. It wanted to see just how smart it was! So it swam around the ocean looking for things to solve. It found a pretty shell on the ocean floor and thought it might be fun to solve a puzzle with it.

The octopus picked up the shell and thought hard. Then it came up with a plan. It made eight tentacles into eight pieces and put them inside the shell. Then it mixed them around so it couldn't tell which pieces were where.

The octopus carefully picked up each of the pieces one by one. To its surprise, it put all the pieces together in the right order! It was so proud of itself that it twirled around with happiness.

The octopus had tested itself and passed with flying colors. It was glad it was so gifted, and it smiled happily.

Once upon a time, there was a boat. The boat was very smelly. It had seen many days of use and was due for a good cleaning.

One day the boat was full of grown-ups and kids. The grown-ups were taking the kids out for a ride on the boat. They had their fun, sailing on the river, but after a while they decided it was time to quit.

The boat was from quit to stop. Everyone jumped off the boat and the boat was left in the water all by itself.

The boat was so smelly. It was making the kids and grown-ups laugh. But it was stuck in the water and couldn't move.

Suddenly, a big running frog hopped onto the boat. He hopped around, cleaning up the smelly mess. He was so strong, he got the boat going in no time!

Everyone was so happy. The boat no longer smelt and they could go back on the river. They thanked the frog and he hopped away back into the bush.

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl. She was three years old and had a sweet tooth. She loved to eat sugary treats all the time.
One day, she found a jar of sugar on the counter. She picked it up and gave it a pinch. Out came some original sugar, and it was just what the little girl wanted!
She reached her tiny hand into the jar and scooped out a big pinch of sugar. She licked it off her fingers and smiled; the sugar was delicious.
With her treat in hand, she ran out of the kitchen and went to show her mom. Her mom said, "Wow, that sugar looks delicious! Where did you get it?"
The little girl smiled and proudly said, "I pinched it from the jar!" Her mom smiled, gave her a hug, and said, "Well, that was very clever of you!"
The little girl smiled and went back outside to play, happy knowing that she had found herself an original tasty treat.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside, even when it was icy and cold. One day, Lily's mom told her to wear her warm coat before going outside. 

Lily didn't want to wear her coat because it made her feel like a big puffy marshmallow. But her mom insisted, saying, "You don't want to catch a cold and need a stitch!" 

Lily didn't understand what her mom meant by "stitch," but she didn't want to get sick. So she put on her coat and went outside to play. 

As she ran around, she saw a little bird shivering in the cold. "Oh no!" said Lily. "The bird is cold like me!" So she ran back inside to get a blanket to wrap around the bird. 

When Lily's mom saw what she did, she smiled and said, "That was very kind of you, Lily. You zipped up the bird just like I asked you to zip up your coat. It's important to take care of others, even when it's cold outside." 

From that day on, Lily always remembered to be kind and caring to others, just like she did for the little bird.

Tweet saw some animals running towards the fire. They were firefighters! They put out the fire and saved the trees. Tweet was so happy and proud of herself for being brave and independent. She knew that she could do anything she believed in.

Sara thinks for a moment. She feels sorry for the flea, but she also feels angry and sore. She does not want to share her fur with the flea. She wants to study and do tricks and be happy.

"Sorry, flea," Sara says. "You cannot stay with me. You have to find another home. Maybe you can find another flea who likes you. But you have to leave me alone."

Sara shakes her fur hard and fast. She makes the flea fly off her back and land on the grass. The flea is sad and confused. It does not understand why Sara does not want it.

So the bunny decided to build a clock. He ran off to his burrow and collected all of the tools he would need. He zipped around collecting twigs and leaves, he zipped around tying bits of string, and he zipped around putting the clock together. 

When the clock was finished, the bunny stood back and admired it. But then he heard a ticking sound coming from the clock! The bunny quickly realised that the clock was ticking away his time.

The bunny smiled knowing the important lesson he had learned. He realised that time was precious and how silly it was to waste it feeling gloomy when there was so much fun and useful things to do.

The bunny zipped off happily, ready to put his lesson into action.

It had broken the fence and was running towards them. Lily and Sam were scared. They jumped off the swings and ran away. But the big dog was faster. It caught up with Lily and bit her leg. Lily screamed and cried. She felt a lot of pain and itch on her leg. She also felt tremble in her body. She was very afraid.

Sam ran to get help. He saw a lady who was walking her small dog. He told her what happened. The lady was kind and brave. She ran to Lily and the big dog. She shouted at the big dog and kicked it away. She picked up Lily and carried her to a bench. She wrapped her leg with a cloth and called for an ambulance. She also gave Lily a hug and told her it was going to be okay.

Lily was still crying and trembling, but she felt a little better. She thanked the lady and her small dog. She also thanked Sam for being a good friend. She hoped the ambulance would come soon and take her to the hospital. She hoped her leg would heal and the itch would go away. She hoped she would never see the big dog again. She learned to be careful around large and mean animals. She also learned to be grateful for kind and brave people.

But then, Sam kicked the ball too hard and it went into the street. Sam ran after the ball without looking. He did not see the big car that was coming fast. The car hit Sam and he fell down. He was hurt and he cried.

Grace saw what happened and she was scared. She ran to Sam and tried to help him. She said, "Sam, Sam, are you okay? Don't cry, I'm here."

Then, she heard a loud noise. It was an ambulance. The ambulance had a red light and a siren. It came to the park and stopped near Sam. Two people came out of the ambulance. They were wearing white clothes and they had a bag. They were doctors.

They went to Sam and looked at him. They said, "Don't worry, Sam, we are here to help you. You are brave and strong. We will take you to the hospital and make you feel better."

They put Sam on a bed with wheels and put him in the ambulance. They said to Grace, "You can come with us, too. You are a good friend to Sam. You can hold his hand and talk to him."

Grace nodded and went in the ambulance with Sam. She held his hand and said, "Sam, I'm sorry you got hurt. I hope you get well soon. I will always be your friend. Do you remember when we played with the ball and had fun?"

Sam smiled and said, "Yes, I remember. You are a good friend, too. Thank you for being with me. You are graceful and kind."

One day, he saw a big boy playing golf with his dad. The big boy had a big golf stick and a big ball. He hit the ball very far and very fast. He made it into the hole every time. Bobby was envious. He wanted to play like the big boy.

"Because I wanted it!" Ben said.

Mom shook her head. She said, "That's not nice, Ben. You made Lily suffer. You should share the tape with her. How would you feel if she took something you liked?"

"I want to be a witch, too!" Ben said. He looked for another black hat, but he could not find one. He saw a red hat, a red cape, and a red mask. He put them on and took another wand. "Abracadabra!"

Lily laughed. "You don't look like a witch! You look like a clown! Witches wear black, not red. You don't match!"

Ben felt sad. He liked his red costume. He thought it was fun and bright. He did not want to change. He said, "I don't care. I like my red costume. I can be a red witch. Red is my favorite color."

Lily shook her head. "No, you can't. Witches are black. You have to match me. We are twins. We have to be the same."

Ben did not agree. He said, "No, we don't. We are twins, but we are not the same. We have different likes and dislikes. We can be different and still be twins. We can be friends and still be different."

Lily thought about it. She realized that Ben was right. She said, "You are right. I'm sorry. I was mean. You can be a red witch if you want. I can be a black witch. We can be different and still be twins. We can be friends and still be different."

Ben smiled. He said, "Thank you. I'm sorry, too. I was sad. You can be a black witch if you want. I can be a red witch. We can be different and still be twins. We can be friends and still be different."

They hugged and said, "We love you, twin!"

They played together happily. They pretended to cast spells and fly on brooms. They had fun with their costumes. They were lucky to have each other.

The moral of the story is: You don't have to match to be friends. You can be different and still be twins. You can be different and still be friends. You can be yourself and still be loved.

Tom and Lily were playing in the park. They liked to swing on the swings and slide on the slides. They saw a big chain on the ground. It was shiny and long.

"Look, a chain!" Tom said. "Let's play with it."

He picked up the chain and wrapped it around his neck. He felt like a king.

"Lily, look at me. I have a chain. I am a king. Clap for me!" he said.

Lily clapped for Tom. She thought he was funny. But then she saw something. A big dog was running towards them. It was barking loud. It wanted the chain.

"Tom, Tom, watch out! A dog!" Lily said. She was worried.

Tom turned around and saw the dog. He was scared. He tried to take off the chain, but it was stuck. The dog was getting closer.

"Help, help!" Tom cried.

Lily ran to Tom. She grabbed the chain and pulled hard. She freed Tom from the chain. She threw the chain away. The dog ran after the chain.

"Come on, Tom, let's go!" Lily said.

They ran to their mom. She was sitting on a bench. She hugged them and kissed them.

"Are you okay, my loves?" she asked.

"Yes, mom, we are okay. But we are sorry. We played with a chain. It was not a good idea. A dog wanted it. It was scary." Tom said.

"It's okay, my loves. I'm glad you are safe. Next time, don't play with things you don't know. They can be dangerous. Now, let's go home and have some cookies." mom said.

Tom and Lily nodded. They held mom's hand and walked home. They learned a lesson. They never played with a chain again.

Rex barked and nodded. He agreed with Ben. They walked home, holding each other. They were happy and safe. The giant was sad and lonely. He wished he had a friend like Rex.

Anna and Ben look at him. They do not know him. They are not sure if they want to share their grill and food. Anna says, "This is our grill. We use it to cook. You can watch, but you cannot touch."

Leo feels sad. He thinks Anna and Ben are not polite. He says, "That is not nice. I want to play, too. Can I have one hamburger, please?"

Ben thinks for a moment. He remembers that his mom always tells him to be kind and share. He says, "Okay, Leo. You can have one hamburger. But you have to ask nicely and say thank you."

Leo smiles. He says, "Thank you, Ben. You are polite. Can I help you cook, too?"

Ben nods. He says, "Sure, Leo. You can use this spatula to flip the burgers. Anna, can you pass the ketchup?"

Anna sees that Leo is friendly and helpful. She says, "Okay, Ben. Here is the ketchup. Leo, do you want some cheese on your burger?"

Leo says, "Yes, please, Anna. You are polite, too. This is fun. Can we be friends?"

Anna and Ben say, "Yes, Leo. We can be friends. We like to play with you. Do you want to play with us tomorrow?"

Leo says, "Yes, I do. I like to play with you, too. You are nice. Thank you for sharing your grill and food."

They all eat their burgers and hot dogs. They laugh and talk. They have a good time. They are happy.

Lily and Max are twins. They like to do everything together. They like to play with their toys, read their books, and watch television. But sometimes they want to watch different things on television.

One day, Lily wants to watch a show about animals. She likes to learn their names and sounds. Max wants to watch a show about cars. He likes to see them race and crash. They both grab the remote and try to change the channel.

"Give me the remote!" Lily says. "I want to watch animals!"

"No, give me the remote!" Max says. "I want to watch cars!"

They pull and tug and push. The remote falls on the floor and breaks. The television goes off. Lily and Max look at each other. They are sad and angry.

Mom hears the noise and comes to the living room. She sees the broken remote and the dark television. She sees Lily and Max with frowns on their faces.

"What happened here?" Mom asks.

"Lily and Max wanted to watch different things on television. They fought over the remote and broke it," Mom says.

"That's not nice. You have to share and take turns. You can't break things when you don't get your way. Now you can't watch anything on television," Mom says.

She picks up the remote and puts it on a high shelf. She tells Lily and Max to separate and go to their rooms. She says they can come out when they are sorry and ready to play nicely.

Lily and Max go to their rooms. They sit on their beds and think. They miss each other. They miss their toys. They miss their television. They realize they were silly and mean. They want to say sorry and hug.

They get up and walk to the door. They open it and see each other. They smile and run to each other. They hug and say sorry.

"I'm sorry, Lily. I love you. You can watch animals next time," Max says.

"I'm sorry, Max. I love you. You can watch cars next time," Lily says.

They go back to the living room. They tell Mom they are sorry and they love her. Mom hugs them and says she is proud of them. She says they can watch television together, but only for a little while. She says they have to play with their toys and read their books too.

Lily and Max agree. They sit on the couch and hold hands. They watch a show that has both animals and cars. They laugh and learn. They are happy and playful. They are twins. They like to do everything together.

"Hello, mouse," Mimi said. "Why are you hiding?"

"Hello, cat," the mouse said. "I'm hiding from the dog. He is big and mean and wants to catch me."

Mimi felt sorry for the mouse. She wanted to help him. She thought of a plan. She said to the mouse, "Don't worry, mouse. I have an idea. Follow me."

Mimi ran towards the dog, making a lot of noise. The dog saw her and chased her. Mimi was fast and smart. She ran around the park, making the dog dizzy. She led the dog to a pond, where a duck was swimming. The duck did not like the dog. He quacked and bit the dog's tail. The dog yelped and ran away.

Mimi ran back to the mouse. The mouse was happy and grateful. He said to Mimi, "Thank you, cat. You are very brave and kind. You saved me from the dog."

Mimi smiled and rubbed her head against the mouse. She said to the mouse, "You're welcome, mouse. You are very sweet and friendly. You can be my friend."

The mouse and the cat became friends. They played and shared in the park. They learned that size and shape do not matter. What matters is being good and helping each other.

He opened the door and saw a dark hole. He was curious and brave, so he went inside. He walked and walked until he came to a bright chamber. It was huge! There were many shiny things inside. There were coins, jewels, crowns, and toys. Ben was amazed. He wanted to play with everything.

He picked up a red car and made it zoom. He put on a golden crown and felt like a king. He grabbed a necklace with a big diamond and put it around his neck. He was having so much fun.

But then he heard a loud roar. He turned around and saw a big dragon. The dragon was angry. He said, "This is my chamber. These are my things. You are a thief. Go away!"

Ben was scared. He dropped the necklace and the crown and the car. He ran back to the door. He locked it with the key and ran out of the hole. He never went back to the chamber again.

He learned a lesson that day. He learned that he should not take things that are not his. He learned that he should value what he has. He learned that some things are more important than shiny things. He learned that he was lucky to have a home, a family, and friends. He learned that he was happy.

Tom is a farmer. He has a big farm with many animals. He likes to feed them and play with them. He has a dog, a cat, a cow, a pig, a horse and a hen.

One day, Tom wakes up early. He sees the sun is bright in the sky. He says, "Good morning, sun! You are very bright today. Let's go to the farm and see the animals."

He goes to the farm and sees the dog. The dog is happy to see Tom. He wags his tail and barks. He says, "Woof, woof, Tom! Can you play with me? I want to run and fetch a stick."

Tom says, "Not now, dog. I have to feed the animals first. Maybe later we can play."

He goes to the cat. The cat is lazy. She lies on the hay and purrs. She says, "Meow, meow, Tom! Can you pet me? I want to feel your hand on my fur."

Tom says, "Not now, cat. I have to feed the animals first. Maybe later I can pet you."

He goes to the cow. The cow is hungry. She moos and chews the grass. She says, "Moo, moo, Tom! Can you milk me? I want to give you some fresh milk."

Tom says, "Not now, cow. I have to feed the animals first. Maybe later I can milk you."

He goes to the pig. The pig is dirty. He rolls in the mud and snorts. He says, "Oink, oink, Tom! Can you wash me? I want to be clean and shiny."

Tom says, "Not now, pig. I have to feed the animals first. Maybe later I can wash you."

He goes to the horse. The horse is strong. He neighs and kicks the fence. He says, "Neigh, neigh, Tom! Can you ride me? I want to gallop and jump."

Tom says, "Not now, horse. I have to feed the animals first. Maybe later I can ride you."

He goes to the hen. The hen is proud. She clucks and lays an egg. She says, "Cluck, cluck, Tom! Can you collect my egg? I want to show you my gift."

Tom says, "Not now, hen. I have to feed the animals first. Maybe later I can collect your egg."

Tom ignores the animals and goes to the barn. He gets some hay, some corn, some carrots, some apples and some seeds. He puts them in a big basket. He says, "Now I can feed the animals. They must be very hungry and thirsty."

He goes back to the farm and feeds the animals. The animals are very happy and grateful. They eat and drink and thank Tom. They say, "Thank you, Tom! You are a good farmer. You take care of us and give us food and water. We love you, Tom!"

Tom smiles and says, "You are welcome, animals! I love you too. You are my friends. Now we can play and have fun."

He plays with the dog, he pets the cat, he milks the cow, he washes the pig, he rides the horse and he collects the hen's egg. He has a great time with the animals. He says, "This is a good day. The sun is bright, the farm is nice and the animals are happy. I am happy too."

Lily liked to touch things. She touched her toys, her books, her clothes, and her cat. She touched everything she saw. But there was one thing she was not allowed to touch. It was a big, round, shiny thing on the wall. It had a number on it. It was zero.

One day, Lily was alone in the living room. She saw the zero thing on the wall. She wanted to touch it. She climbed on the sofa and reached for it. She touched it with her finger. It made a loud noise. It was a fire alarm.

Lily was scared. She jumped off the sofa and ran to the door. She saw her mom and dad coming. They looked angry and worried. They saw the fire alarm and the smoke. They saw Lily.

"Lily, what did you do?" Mom asked.

"I touched the zero thing," Lily said.

"Why did you touch it? You know you are not supposed to touch it. It is for emergencies only. It is unusual and dangerous. It makes the firemen come. They think there is a fire. You made a big mistake," Dad said.

Lily felt bad. She did not know the zero thing was unusual and dangerous. She did not know it made the firemen come. She did not want to make a mistake. She wanted to say sorry.

"I'm sorry, Mom. I'm sorry, Dad. I won't touch the zero thing again. I promise," Lily said.

Mom and Dad hugged Lily. They were not angry anymore. They were glad Lily was safe. They explained to the firemen what happened. The firemen were nice. They told Lily to be careful and to listen to her parents. They left.

Lily learned a lesson. She still liked to touch things. But she did not touch the zero thing anymore. She touched other things that were fun and safe. She was happy.

"Oh no, we have to go down!" Lila said. She felt sorry for making her mom worry.

They tried to go down, but it was hard. They slipped and scratched their hands and legs. They cried and called for help.

Lily wanted to cheer her up, so she took her by the hand and led her to her room. She showed her all her drawings on the wall and told her stories about them. Grandma listened and nodded and said they were very beautiful and clever. She pointed to one drawing of a big red heart and said it was her favorite.

Lily and Tom were twins who liked to observe things. They had a big book with pictures of animals, plants, and stars. Every day, they would look at the book and learn new words.

One day, they decided to observe the sky. They went outside with their book and a blanket. They lay down on the grass and looked up. The sky was blue and bright. They saw some white clouds and a yellow sun.

"Look, Lily, a bird!" Tom said, pointing at a black shape in the air.

"Wow, a bird!" Lily said, trying to find it in the book. "What kind of bird is it?"

"I don't know. Maybe a crow. It has a big beak and a loud voice."

They watched the bird fly across the sky. It made a caw-caw sound. They tried to imitate it.

Suddenly, the sky turned dark. The sun was gone. The clouds were gray and thick. The bird was quiet.

"What happened, Tom?" Lily asked, feeling scared.

"I don't know, Lily. Maybe it's night. But it was day a minute ago."

They heard a rumble in the sky. It sounded like thunder. They saw a flash of light. It looked like lightning.

"Let's go inside, Lily. It's not safe here." Tom said, grabbing the book and the blanket.

They ran to the house, holding hands. They saw their mom at the door. She looked worried.

"Mom, what's going on?" Lily asked.

"It's a solar eclipse, kids. It's when the moon covers the sun for a little while. It makes the day dark and quiet. But don't worry, it will be over soon. Come inside and I'll explain more." Mom said, hugging them.

They went inside and sat on the couch. Mom showed them a picture of a solar eclipse in the book. She told them it was a rare and special event. She said they were lucky to observe it.

Lily and Tom felt better. They learned something new. They waited for the day to come back. They hoped to see the bird again.

"What is this?" she asked. "This is not a flower. This is a seed. I don't want to see a seed. I want to see flowers."

She was about to close the book when she heard a voice.

"Wait!" the voice said. "Don't close the book. I have something to show you."

Sara was surprised. She looked around, but she did not see anyone. She looked at the book, but she did not see anyone. She wondered who was talking.

"Who are you?" she asked. "Where are you?"

"I am the seed," the voice said. "I am on the page. I am in the book. I am talking to you."

Sara was amazed. She had never heard a seed talk before. She looked at the seed again. It still looked boring.

"Why are you talking to me?" she asked. "What do you want to show me?"

"I want to show you how I bloom," the seed said. "I want to show you how I become a flower. I want to show you how I change and grow. It is a very serious thing. It is a very wonderful thing. Will you watch me?"

Sara was curious. She wanted to see how a seed became a flower. She wanted to see how it changed and grew. She wanted to see something wonderful.

"Okay," she said. "I will watch you. How do you bloom?"

"Turn the page," the seed said. "And you will see."

Anna nodded. She was curious. She followed her aunt to a room. The room had a big window. Anna saw something outside. It was a small house with a door and a window. It was pink and white. It had flowers and a sign. The sign said, "Anna's house".

Anna gasped. She was amazed. She said, "Is that for me?"

Aunt Lisa smiled. She said, "Yes, it is. I made it for you. Do you like it?"

Anna nodded. She was very happy. She said, "I love it! Thank you, aunt Lisa!"

Aunt Lisa said, "You're welcome, sweetie. Do you want to go inside?"

Anna nodded. She ran to the door. She opened it. She saw a table and chairs, a bed and a closet, a rug and a lamp. She saw a doll and a teddy bear, a tea set and a book. She saw a picture of her and her aunt.

Anna smiled. She said, "This is the best house ever!"

Aunt Lisa said, "I'm glad you like it. Do you want to play with me?"

Anna nodded. She said, "Yes, please!"

Aunt Lisa said, "Okay, let's play. I'll be your guest. Do you want to offer me some tea?"

Anna nodded. She said, "Yes, I do!"

She picked up the tea pot. She poured some tea. She gave a cup to her aunt. She said, "Here you go, aunt Lisa. This is the best tea ever!"

Aunt Lisa said, "Thank you, Anna. This is the best tea ever!"

They drank the tea. They talked and laughed. They had a lot of fun. They played until it was time to go.

Anna hugged her aunt. She said, "Thank you for the house, aunt Lisa. I love you!"

Aunt Lisa hugged her back. She said, "You're welcome, Anna. I love you too!"

Anna and her mom said goodbye to her aunt. They went home. Anna was very happy. She had the best day ever. She had the best aunt ever. She had the best house ever.

One day, Ben and Lily saw the big dog again. He was not on a leash. He ran towards them. Ben and Lily were scared. They ran to the slide. They hoped the big dog would not follow them.

But the big dog was fast. He jumped on the slide. He tried to bite Ben and Lily. Ben and Lily screamed. They slid down the slide. They looked for a place to hide.

They saw a tent. The tent was near the slide. The tent was blue and yellow. It had a zip. Ben and Lily ran to the tent. They opened the zip. They went inside. They closed the zip.

They waited. They heard the big dog outside. He sniffed and scratched. He wanted to get in. Ben and Lily hugged each other. They wished the big dog would go away.

Then they heard a voice. The voice was kind. The voice said, "Hey, what are you doing in my tent?" Ben and Lily looked up. They saw a man. The man was tall and strong. He had a hat and a badge. He was a park ranger.

The park ranger smiled. He said, "Don't be afraid. I'm here to help. I know the big dog. He is not mean. He is just playful. He likes to zip around the park. He does not know how to be gentle. I will teach him. Come on, let's go out and meet him."

Ben and Lily were not sure. They were still scared. But they trusted the park ranger. He seemed kind. They opened the zip. They went out of the tent.

The park ranger held the big dog. He said, "This is Rex. He is my friend. He is sorry for scaring you. He wants to say hello. Can you give him a pat?" He showed Ben and Lily how to pat the big dog.

Ben and Lily were brave. They patted the big dog. The big dog licked their faces. He wagged his tail. He was not a threat. He was a friend.

Ben and Lily smiled. They said, "Hello, Rex. We are Ben and Lily. We like to play in the park. Do you want to play with us?" Rex barked. He nodded. He wanted to play.

The park ranger said, "That's great. I'm glad you made a new friend. But remember, always be careful around dogs you don't know. And always ask their owners before you touch them. OK?" Ben and Lily nodded. They said, "OK."

They thanked the park ranger. They said goodbye to Rex. They went back to the slide. They had fun. They zipped down the slide. They laughed. They were happy.

Cara and Drumby decided to have a race. Cara thought she would win because she was so fast. Drumby knew he was slow, but he wanted to have fun. They started the race, and Cara zoomed ahead. She was so sure she would win that she stopped to take a nap.

Drumby kept going, playing his rhythm as he moved. He did not stop or go fast. He just kept a steady pace. As Cara slept, Drumby passed her. When Cara woke up, she saw Drumby near the finish line. She tried to catch up, but it was too late. Drumby won the race.

Cara learned that being impatient and going too fast is not always the best way. Sometimes, it is better to be slow and steady, like Drumby. Cara and Drumby became good friends, and they taught each other how to be both fast and steady. And they lived happily ever after.

"Oh no! We need to get out of the pond!" yelled Ducky.

Sue smiled and started to pretend she had a balloon. They played together, laughing and having fun. They learned that they didn't need real balloons to be happy. All they needed was their imagination and a good friend to share it with.

The moral of the story is that sometimes, all you need is a little bit of imagination and a good friend to have fun and be happy.

Once upon a time, in a big green park, there was a small red ball. The red ball loved to roll on the grass. One sunny day, the red ball met a tall palm tree. The palm tree had big leaves that danced in the wind. The red ball wanted to play with the palm tree.

The red ball decided to roll very fast towards the palm tree. It rolled and rolled until it bumped into the trunk. The palm tree shook, and some of its leaves fell to the ground. The palm tree was angry at the red ball for making its leaves fall.

The red ball felt sad and said sorry to the palm tree. The palm tree forgave the red ball, and they became friends. From that day on, the red ball learned to roll gently and play nicely with the palm tree and all the other trees in the park. They all lived happily together.

One day, Tom saw a big box in the living room. He wanted to know what was inside. So, he jumped off the couch and went to the box. He tried to open it, but it was too hard for him.

Tom's friend, a little girl named Lucy, came to help. Together, they opened the box and found a puzzle. They worked together to complete the puzzle. When they were done, they were so happy. They put the puzzle on the couch to show everyone. From that day on, Tom and Lucy were the best of friends.

Once upon a time, there was a pretty bird who loved to whistle. Every day, the bird would sit on a tree branch and whistle a happy song. All the animals in the forest would stop and listen to the bird's beautiful tunes.

One day, as the bird was getting ready to whistle its song, it saw a big, yummy lunch on the ground. The bird was very hungry, so it flew down from the tree to eat the lunch. The bird was so excited about the food that it forgot to whistle its song.

As the bird ate the lunch, a sneaky cat came closer and closer. The other animals in the forest were waiting for the bird's whistle, but they didn't hear it. They knew something was wrong. Just in time, the animals ran to help the bird. They scared the sneaky cat away, and the bird was safe. From that day on, the pretty bird always whistled its song before eating lunch, so the animals knew it was safe and happy.

Her mom said, "That is a microscope. We use it to measure and look at things that are very small."

Amy wanted to see what she could find with the microscope. She looked around the house for things to measure. She found a tiny bug and put it under the microscope. She was excited to see what it looked like up close.

Amy's friend, Ben, came over to play. He saw the microscope and asked, "What are you doing?"

Amy told him, "I am using this microscope to measure a tiny bug. It is fun! You can try it too."

Ben and Amy took turns using the microscope. They looked at many small things and had a great time. They were happy that the microscope was available for them to use.

One time, the ball rolled near a big tree. Tim ran to get it, but he saw something shiny under the leaves. He bent down and picked it up. It was a whistle. It was red and yellow and had a string. Tim blew the whistle and it made a loud noise.

"Wow, look what I found!" Tim shouted to Lily. "A whistle!"

Lily ran over to see. She wanted to try the whistle too. She asked Tim to share it with her.

"Please, can I have a turn?" Lily said.

"OK, but only one turn," Tim said. He gave the whistle to Lily. Lily blew the whistle and it made a loud noise too.

They both laughed and smiled. They liked the whistle. They decided to play a game with it. They took turns hiding the whistle and making the other one guess where it was.

They had fun playing the game, but they did not notice that they were making too much noise. They did not see the old man who lived in the house next to the park. He was trying to take a nap, but he could not sleep because of the whistle. He was very angry. He opened his window and shouted at them.

"Hey, you naughty children! Stop that noise! Give me that whistle!" he yelled.

Tim and Lily were scared. They did not know the old man was there. They did not mean to be naughty. They dropped the whistle and ran away. They left the ball and the whistle behind. They ran back to their mom, who was sitting on a bench.

"Mom, mom, there was a mean man who yelled at us!" they cried.

Mom hugged them and asked them what happened. They told her about the whistle and the game and the old man. Mom listened and shook her head.

"You should not have taken the whistle. It was not yours. Maybe it belonged to someone else. And you should not have made so much noise. You disturbed the old man. He was not mean, he was just tired. You were naughty," she said.

Tim and Lily felt sorry. They did not want to be naughty. They wanted to be good. They asked Mom what they should do.

"You should go back and say sorry to the old man. And you should give him the whistle. Maybe he will forgive you. And you should take your ball too. It is yours," she said.

Tim and Lily nodded. They were afraid, but they wanted to do the right thing. They held Mom's hand and walked back to the tree. They saw the old man standing there. He had the whistle and the ball in his hands. He looked grumpy.

Tim and Lily swallowed hard. They walked up to him and said in a small voice:

"Sorry, sir. We did not mean to take your whistle. We did not mean to make noise. We were playing a game. Please, can we have our ball back?"

The old man looked at them. He saw that they were sorry. He softened a little. He gave them their ball back.

"It's OK, kids. I accept your apology. But you should be more careful next time. The whistle is not mine either. I found it here too. I don't know who it belongs to. Maybe you can keep it. But don't blow it too loud. And don't bother me again. I need my nap," he said.

Tim and Lily thanked him. They took the ball and the whistle. They promised to be quiet and not to bother him again. They walked back to Mom. They told her what the old man said. Mom smiled and praised them.

"You did well, kids. You were brave and polite. You learned your lesson. Now, let's go home and have some cookies. And maybe you can play with the whistle later. But only in the backyard," she said.

Tim and Lily agreed. They were happy. They hugged Mom and followed her home. They learned to be good and not to be naughty. They still liked the whistle, but they knew when to use it and when not to. They had a good day.

The little girl wanted to go swim in the water, but her mommy and daddy told her that they didn't have any floaties available. So, they decided to build sandcastles instead. They worked hard on building a big castle with towers and a moat. It was so much fun! 

After they finished playing, they packed up their things and went home. The little girl was so tired from playing all day that she fell asleep in the car. When they got home, her mommy and daddy carried her to bed and she dreamt about the fun day they had at the beach.

He went back to playing with his other toys and started to create something new. He used his creative mind to make a toy gun out of cardboard and markers. A few days later, Timmy's friend came over to play. Timmy showed him his new toy gun and they played together. Timmy's friend was impressed with how creative Timmy was. They had so much fun playing with the toy gun that they forgot about the pistol in the store. Timmy realized that he didn't need to buy things to have fun, he could just use his imagination and create something new.

His toys were ruined, and he had no one to blame but himself.

Grandpa came and saw what happened. He was very angry with Tom, and he scolded him. He said Tom was selfish and mean, and he had to learn to share and respect. He said Tom had to apologize to the sheep, and help him fix his toys. He also said Tom had to take a bath, because he was smelly too. Tom felt very sorry and ashamed. He did what grandpa said, and he promised to be a better boy. He learned his lesson, and he never tried to take what was not his again.

"Rot is when something is not good anymore. It is not fresh. It is not nice. It is like this pumpkin," Pam says.

"Why is it rot?" Tim asks.

"Because it is too long here. It is too hot and too light. The sun makes it rot. The sun is high and bright. It is noon," Pam says.

"Noon? What is noon?" Tim asks.

"Noon is when the sun is in the middle of the sky. It is the middle of the day. It is very light and very hot. It is not good for pumpkins," Pam says.

"Can we make it not rot?" Tim asks.

"No, we cannot. It is too late. We have to throw it away. It is not good for us. It can make us sick," Pam says.

Lily and Tom ran as fast as they could. They reached the door and opened it. They ran out of the palace and back to the park. They were very happy and relieved. Sam and Mia liked to play in the park. They liked to swing, slide and run. But their favorite thing was to make mud pies. They would find a wet spot and dig with their hands. Then they would shape the mud into pies and put them on a big rock.

One day, they saw a new sign in the park. It said: "Please do not make mud pies. They are messy and bad for the grass." Sam and Mia did not understand. They liked mud pies. They were fun and good for the rock.

They decided to ask their mom. She was sitting on a bench and reading a book. They ran to her and showed her the sign. "Mom, why can't we make mud pies?" they asked.

Mom looked at the sign and sighed. She put down her book and tried to explain. "Mud pies are not really pies, you know. They are just dirt and water. They do not taste good and they do not last long. They also make a lot of mess. They stick to your clothes and shoes and hands. They also make the grass brown and sad. The grass needs water and sun to grow green and happy. If you make mud pies, you take away the water and cover the sun. That is why the sign says no mud pies."

Sam and Mia listened to mom. They felt frustrated. They did not want to make the grass sad. But they also did not want to stop making mud pies. They liked mud pies. They were fun and good for the rock. They did not know what to do.

Mom saw their faces and smiled. She had an idea. "How about this?" she said. "You can still make mud pies, but only in a special place. We can find a spot where there is no grass, only dirt. We can also bring a bucket and a hose. You can use the bucket to make mud and the hose to clean up. That way, you can have fun and not make a mess. What do you think?"

Sam and Mia liked mom's idea. They thought it was fair and smart. They thanked mom and hugged her. Then they ran to find a spot for their mud pies. They were happy and excited. They did not mind the sign anymore. They had a new way to play.

One day, Sara and Ben decide to do something fun with their lovely blanket. They put it over their bed and make a tent. They crawl inside and pretend they are camping. They tell stories and sing songs. They have a lot of fun.

But then, they hear their mom calling them. It is time for lunch. Sara and Ben do not want to leave their tent. They want to play more. They say to their mom, "Please, can we stay a little longer?"

Their mom smiles and says, "Okay, but only for a little while. Then you have to come and eat. And you have to share your lovely blanket with me. I want to see it too."

Sara and Ben agree. They say, "Okay, mom. We will share our lovely blanket with you. It is very nice. You will like it."

They hug their mom and go back to their tent. They are happy. They love their lovely blanket. And they love their mom.

They made a note with crayons that said "Toys for sale. One coin each." They put the note on the box and waited for customers.

Soon, a boy named Sam came by. He saw the note and the toys and stopped. He liked a red car that was in the box. He asked Lily and Tom, "Can I have this car?"

Lily and Tom nodded. "Yes, you can. But you have to give us one coin," they said.

Sam looked in his pocket. He had two coins. He gave one coin to Lily and Tom and took the car. He was happy.

Then, a girl named Mia came by. She saw the note and the toys and stopped. She liked a yellow doll that was in the box. She asked Lily and Tom, "Can I have this doll?"

Lily and Tom nodded. "Yes, you can. But you have to give us one coin," they said.

Mia looked in her pocket. She had no coins. She was sad.

She saw a mighty rock that was on the ground. It was big and shiny. She picked it up and said, "Can I trade this rock for the doll?"

Lily and Tom looked at the rock. They liked it. It was mighty. They said, "OK, you can trade. We will take the rock and you can have the doll."

Mia gave them the rock and took the doll. She was happy.

Lily and Tom put the rock in the box. They had one coin and one rock. They were happy.

They sold their toys and made new friends. They had fun.

"Let's go home, Tom. There is a storm," Mia says.

"No, I want to play more. The storm is fun," Tom says. He insists. He is careless.

Mia is scared. She does not like the storm. She sees a big flash. She hears a boom. She cries.

"Tom, please, come with me. The storm is not fun. The storm is dangerous," Mia says.

Tom sees Mia cry. He feels sorry. He is not careless anymore. He holds Mia's hand. They run to their homes. They are safe.

The storm goes away. The sun comes out. Tom and Mia hug. They are friends. They are happy.

One night, she saw a big star that was brighter than the others. She thought it was a special star. She stretched her arm as far as she could and said, "Please, star, let me have a wish. I wish I could fly to you and see what you are like."

Suddenly, she felt a warm breeze lift her up. She was flying in the air, closer and closer to the star. She was so happy and excited. She felt like she was in a dream.

She reached the star and touched it gently. It was soft and warm and sparkled. The star smiled at her and said, "Hello, Lila. I heard your wish and I wanted to meet you. You are a brave and kind girl. I have a gift for you. Close your eyes and make another wish."

Lila closed her eyes and thought hard. She wished for something that would make her and everyone happy. She wished for a peaceful world, where there was no fighting, no hurting, no crying. She wished for love and joy and friendship.

She opened her eyes and saw the star glow brighter. The star said, "Your wish is beautiful, Lila. I will help you make it come true. But first, you have to go back to your home and sleep. Be good and kind and brave, and you will spread peace and happiness."

He picked up the magnet and looked at it. He saw a small switch on the side. He pushed the switch and heard a click. Suddenly, the magnet became very strong. It pulled the fridge door and made a loud noise. Sam was scared.

He tried to pull the magnet away, but it was too hard. He saw the fridge door bend and crack. He saw the food and drinks fall out. He saw the milk carton explode and make a mess. He heard his mom scream.

He wished he had not played with the magnet. He wished he had listened to his dad. He wished he could make it stop. He wished he could disappear.

But then, something unusual happened. A loud noise came from the wall. It was an alarm. It went beep beep beep. Lily and Ben woke up. They were scared. What was the alarm for?

They got out of their beds and ran to their mom and dad. Mom and dad were also awake. They heard the alarm too. They hugged Lily and Ben and said, "Don't worry, it's just a fire drill. We have to go outside and wait until it stops."

They put on their coats and shoes and followed mom and dad. They saw other people and kids going outside too. They all looked sleepy and confused. The alarm was still beeping.

They waited outside for a long time. It was cold and dark. Lily and Ben held their teddy bears and blankets. They wished they could go back to sleep.

Finally, the alarm stopped. A man with a hat and a badge said, "It's OK, everyone. It was a false alarm. There is no fire. You can go back to your rooms now. Sorry for the trouble."

Mom and dad said, "Thank you, sir. Come on, Lily and Ben. Let's go back to bed. It's late."

They went back to their room. They got into their beds. They were tired and happy. They said, "Good night, mom and dad. Good night, teddy bears. Good night, alarm."

They closed their eyes and fell asleep. They hoped nothing unusual would happen again.

Lily loved flowers. She liked to look at them, smell them, and touch them. She had a small garden in her backyard, where she planted seeds and watered them every day. She was very happy when the seeds grew into green stems and leaves.

One day, she saw a new flower in her garden. It was pink and round, with many petals. It looked like a ball of cotton candy. Lily wanted to pick it and put it in a vase. She ran to the flower and reached for it.

"Stop!" a voice said. Lily looked around and saw a fairy sitting on the flower. The fairy had wings like a butterfly and a dress like a leaf. She looked angry.

"This is my flower," the fairy said. "You can't take it. It is mine."

Lily was surprised. She had never seen a fairy before. She thought fairies were nice and friendly. She did not understand why the fairy was so mean.

"But I like this flower," Lily said. "It is so pretty. I want to have it in my room."

"No, you can't," the fairy said. "This flower is special. It only blooms once a year. If you pick it, it will die. You have to leave it alone."

Lily felt sad. She really wanted the flower. She thought it would make her happy. She did not care if it died. She was stubborn. She tried to grab the flower again.

The fairy saw her and flew in front of her. She waved her wand and sprinkled some dust on Lily. Lily felt a tickle on her nose. She sneezed. When she opened her eyes, she saw that she had turned into a flower. She was stuck in the ground, next to the pink flower.

"What did you do?" Lily cried. "Change me back!"

"Sorry, I can't," the fairy said. "You have to learn your lesson. You have to respect nature and other living things. You can't be selfish and greedy. You have to stay here until the next time this flower blooms. Then you will be free."

Lily was scared. She did not want to be a flower. She wanted to be a girl. She wanted to go back to her house, her family, and her toys. She wanted to hug her teddy bear and sleep in her bed. She wished she had listened to the fairy.

She looked at the pink flower and saw that it was smiling. It did not seem to mind being a flower. It was happy and peaceful. It spoke to Lily in a soft voice.

"Hello, friend," it said. "Don't be sad. Being a flower is not so bad. You can see the sun, the sky, and the stars. You can feel the wind, the rain, and the dew. You can smell the other flowers, the grass, and the earth. You can hear the birds, the bees, and the fairy. You can grow, bloom, and fade. You can be part of the cycle of life. You can be beautiful and free."

Lily listened to the flower. She did not understand everything it said. But she felt something in her chest. It was warm and calm. It was like a hug. She smiled back at the flower. She decided to give it a chance. She decided to be a flower for a while. She decided to be a friend.

Timmy and Lily were playing in the garden. They liked to dig in the dirt and look for bugs. They also liked to eat snacks that Mommy gave them.

"Look, Timmy, I have grapes!" Lily said, holding a bunch of red grapes in her hand. "Do you want some?"

"No, thank you, Lily. I hate grapes. They are sour and yucky. I like bananas. They are sweet and soft." Timmy said, making a face.

"But grapes are good for you. They have juice and vitamins. And they are red, like your shirt. Don't you like red?" Lily asked, trying to share her grapes with Timmy.

"I like red, but not on grapes. Red is for fire trucks and apples and balloons. Grapes should be green or purple. Red grapes are wrong." Timmy said, shaking his head.

Lily was sad. She liked red grapes. She thought they were pretty and tasty. She did not understand why Timmy hated them. She wanted to play with him, but he did not want her grapes.

"Fine, Timmy. You can have your bananas. I will eat my grapes by myself. And I will find a new friend who likes red grapes too." Lily said, walking away with her grapes.

Timmy felt sorry. He did not mean to hurt Lily's feelings. He liked to play with her, but he did not like her grapes. He wished he could like them, but he could not.

"Wait, Lily. I'm sorry. I don't hate you. I just hate grapes. Can we still be friends?" Timmy called out, running after Lily.

Lily stopped and turned around. She saw Timmy's sad face. She felt sorry too. She did not want to lose Timmy as a friend. She liked him, even if he did not like her grapes.

"Okay, Timmy. We can still be friends. But you have to try one grape. Just one. Maybe you will like it. Please?" Lily said, holding out a grape to Timmy.

Timmy looked at the grape. He did not want to try it. He was sure he would hate it. But he wanted to make Lily happy. He wanted to be a good friend. He took a deep breath and bit the grape.

He was surprised. The grape was not sour and yucky. It was sweet and juicy. It was not wrong. It was good.

"Mmm, this is good. I like it. I don't hate grapes anymore. I like red grapes. Thank you, Lily." Timmy said, smiling.

Lily smiled too. She was happy. She gave Timmy another grape. They ate their grapes and bananas together. They were friends again. They played in the garden until Mommy called them for lunch.

One day, Bella saw a big pile of hay in the barn. She was very hungry and wanted to eat some. She looked around and saw no one. She thought, maybe I can take a little bit. No one will know. She walked to the hay and took a big bite.

But then she heard a voice. "Hey, that's my hay!" It was Rocky, the horse. He was very angry. He ran to the barn and saw Bella with hay in her mouth. "You are a bad cow! You stole my hay! That hay is for me and my friends, not for you!"

Bella felt guilty. She knew she did something wrong. She wanted to say sorry, but she was too scared. She ran away from Rocky and hid behind a tree.

Lila and Milo saw what happened. They felt sorry for Bella. They knew she was hungry and made a mistake. They decided to help her. They went to Rocky and said, "Rocky, please don't be mad at Bella. She is our friend. She was hungry and did not know that hay was yours. She is very sorry. Can you forgive her?"

Rocky was still angry, but he also felt a little sorry. He liked Bella, too. He said, "Well, I guess I can forgive her. But she has to promise not to take my hay again. And she has to share some of her hay with me and my friends, too."

Lila and Milo nodded. They went to find Bella and told her what Rocky said. Bella was happy and relieved. She said, "Thank you, Lila and Milo. You are very good friends. You protected me from Rocky. I am sorry, Rocky. I will not take your hay again. And I will share some of my hay with you and your friends, too."

Rocky smiled. He said, "Thank you, Bella. You are a good cow. You learned your lesson. Come on, let's all eat some hay together."

Bella, Lila, Milo, and Rocky went to the barn and ate some hay together. They were all happy and full. They learned to share and forgive. They were good friends.

Tim and Sam were brothers who liked to play with cars. They had many cars of different colors and sizes. They liked to race them on the floor and make loud noises. One day, they found a big car in the garage. It was their dad's car. It was red and shiny and had four doors.

"Wow, look at this car!" Tim said. "It is so big and fast. I want to drive it."

"Me too!" Sam said. "But we are too small. We can't reach the pedals or the wheel."

Tim had an idea. He saw a box in the corner. He dragged it to the car and climbed on it. He opened the door and got inside. He could see the wheel and the buttons. He felt jolly.

"Look at me, Sam!" Tim said. "I am in the car. I can drive it. Come and join me."

Sam was not sure. He thought it was dangerous. He saw a sign on the car that said "gas". He knew gas was something that made the car go. He wondered if there was gas in the car.

"Tim, be careful!" Sam said. "You don't know how to drive. You might break the car. Or worse, you might hurt yourself or me."

"Don't be silly, Sam!" Tim said. "It is easy. You just push this button and turn this wheel. And then you go zoom, zoom, zoom. It is fun. Don't be scared. Come and join me."

Tim pushed the button. The car made a loud noise. It started to move. Tim was surprised. He did not know how to stop it. He turned the wheel. The car went left and right. It bumped into the wall. It bumped into the bike. It bumped into the trash can. Tim was scared. He screamed.

"Help, help, help!" Tim said. "I can't stop the car. It is going too fast. It is out of control. Help, help, help!"

Sam heard Tim's scream. He ran to the car. He saw Tim in trouble. He wanted to help him. He climbed on the box and got inside. He saw a pedal on the floor. He pushed it with his foot. The car stopped. Tim was relieved. He hugged Sam.

"Thank you, thank you, thank you!" Tim said. "You saved me. You stopped the car. You are a hero. You succeeded."

Sam smiled. He was glad he helped Tim. He was glad they were safe. He hugged Tim back.

"You're welcome, you're welcome, you're welcome!" Sam said. "You are my brother. I love you. You are brave. You tried."

They got out of the car. They saw the mess they made. They felt sorry. They heard their dad coming. They were afraid. They ran to their room. They hid under the bed. They hoped their dad would not be angry. They learned a lesson. They never played with the car again.

"What is that?" Lily asked.

"Can we play with it?" Sam asked.

"No, you can't," dad said. "It is not safe to play with a jellyfish. It might hurt you or make you sick. You have to stay away from it and let it be."

Lily and Sam nodded. They did not want to get stung by the jellyfish. They wanted to have fun and be safe. They decided to play with their buckets and shovels instead. Lily and Ben were playing with their dolls in the garden. They liked to pretend that their dolls were friends who went on adventures together. Lily had a pink doll with long hair and a dress. Ben had a blue doll with short hair and a cap.

"Let's go to the park and see the animals," Lily said to Ben.

"Okay, that sounds fun," Ben said. They picked up their dolls and walked to the park.

At the park, they saw a big dog with a collar and a leash. The dog was barking and jumping. Lily and Ben were scared of the dog. They hid behind a bench and hugged their dolls.

"Shh, don't make noise," Lily whispered to Ben. "Maybe the dog will go away."

But the dog did not go away. It saw Lily and Ben and ran towards them. It wanted to play with them and their dolls. It poked Lily's doll with its nose and made it fall on the ground. Then it poked Ben's doll with its paw and made it fly in the air.

"Hey, stop that!" Ben shouted at the dog. "You are hurting our dolls!"

The dog did not understand. It thought Ben was playing too. It wagged its tail and barked louder.

Lily and Ben were very upset. They cried and called for help. A man came running to them. He was the dog's owner. He was a judge. He wore a black robe and a white wig. He looked very serious and important.

"I'm sorry, kids," the judge said. "My dog didn't mean to hurt your dolls. He just wanted to say hello. He is very friendly and compassionate. He loves everyone."

The judge picked up Lily's doll and Ben's doll and gave them back to the kids. He brushed off the dirt and the grass from the dolls. He smiled and said, "There, they are fine. No harm done. Do you want to pet my dog? He is very soft and gentle."

Lily and Ben looked at the judge and his dog. They were still scared, but they also felt curious. The judge and his dog seemed nice and kind. They decided to give them a chance.

"Okay, we will pet your dog," Lily said. "But only if he doesn't poke our dolls again."

"Deal," the judge said. He held his dog's leash and let Lily and Ben touch his fur. The dog licked their hands and wagged his tail. He was happy to make new friends.

Lily and Ben smiled and laughed. They felt better. They thanked the judge and his dog for being compassionate. They learned that sometimes things are not as scary as they seem. They also learned that poking is not a good way to say hello.

"Help, help!" Jill and Ben cried. "We are lost on the ocean!"

But no one heard them. No one came to help them. They were alone on the boat. They were scared and hungry and cold. They hugged each other tight and wished they had listened to their mom and dad.

The moral of the story is: Do not go too far from the shore. The ocean can be dangerous. Listen to your mom and dad. They know what is best for you.

Lisa was a very intelligent girl. She liked to read books, solve puzzles and learn new things. She always did her best at school and at home. But sometimes, she felt very tired and stressed. She had too much work and not enough play.

One day, she came home from school with a big headache. She had a lot of homework to do, but she could not concentrate. She felt angry and sad. She threw her books on the floor and started to cry.

Her mother heard her and came to her room. She saw Lisa crying and hugged her. She said, "Lisa, what is wrong? Why are you so upset?"

Lisa said, "I have too much work, Mom. I can't do it all. I want to be the best, but I feel so bad."

Her mother said, "Lisa, you are a very intelligent girl, but you need to relax. You can't do everything at once. You need to take a break and have some fun. You need to be kind to yourself."

She took Lisa to the bathroom and filled the tub with warm water. She added some bubbles and a rubber duck. She said, "Lisa, why don't you take a bath and play with your duck? It will make you feel better. I will help you with your homework later."

Lisa nodded and smiled. She got into the tub and splashed the water. She played with her duck and made it quack. She felt her headache go away. She felt calm and happy.

Her mother came back and gave her a towel. She said, "Lisa, you look much better. How do you feel?"

Lisa said, "I feel good, Mom. Thank you for helping me. I love you."

Her mother said, "I love you too, Lisa. You are a very intelligent girl, but you also need to relax. Relaxing is good for your mind and your body. It helps you to learn and to grow. Remember, you don't have to be perfect. You just have to be yourself."

She gave Lisa a rub on her back and a kiss on her cheek. She said, "Now, let's go and do your homework together. We can make it fun and easy."

Lisa nodded and hugged her mother. She said, "Okay, Mom. Let's go."

They went to Lisa's room and did her homework. They laughed and talked and learned. Lisa felt proud and happy. She learned that relaxing is important and that she can always ask for help. She learned to be kind to herself and to others. She learned a valuable lesson.

He ran back to the living room, where Lily was waiting. He put the new battery in her car and closed the door. He gave her the car and said, "Here you go, Lily. Try it now."

Lily and Tommy decided to take the box to their parents. They showed them the box and asked for their help. The parents opened the box, and inside, they found a cute little puppy. The mystery was solved, and Lily and Tommy were happy to have a new friend to play with.

Once upon a time, there was a little lamb named Lily. Lily had soft, white wool that her mommy liked to brush every day. One day, Lily saw a big, blue butterfly and she wanted to catch it. So, she ran after it and soon she was lost.

Lily was scared and didn't know what to do. Suddenly, she heard a whisper. "Hello?" she said. "Who's there?" A big, scary wolf appeared. "I am here to eat you," he said.

Lily was too scared to move, and the wolf ate her up. Her mommy never found her, and she was very sad. From then on, she always kept a close eye on her other little lambs.

Finally, the bear gave up and went away. The deer was safe and happy that he found a seat to hide behind. From that day on, he always remembered to be careful when he was looking for food.

The bee did not like Tom's words. He said, "You are a silly ant. You know nothing. The shiny thing is mine, and I will not share it. Now go away, or I will sting you!"

Tom was brave, but he was also smart. He knew he could not fight the bee, but he had an idea. He said, "OK, I will go away, but can I ask you one thing? Can you show me how you shine like the shiny thing? You are so bright and beautiful, I want to learn from you."
