One day, a boy named Tom went to the beach with his mom and dad. He liked to play in the sand and look for shells and rocks. He saw a big brown octopus on the shore. It was not moving. Tom wanted to touch it.

"Mom, can I touch the octopus?" he asked.

"No, Tom, you can't. It might be sick or hurt. It might bite you. Leave it alone," his mom said.

But Tom did not listen. He ran to the octopus and lay down next to it. He reached out his hand and poked it. The octopus opened its eyes and wrapped its arms around Tom. It squeezed him hard. Tom screamed and cried.

"Help, help, the octopus is hurting me!" he shouted.

His mom and dad heard him and ran to him. They pulled the octopus off him and threw it back into the water. They hugged Tom and checked him for wounds. He had some red marks on his skin, but he was not bleeding.

"Tom, you are very lucky. The octopus could have hurt you more. Why did you not listen to me?" his mom asked.

"I'm sorry, mom. I was curious. I wanted to touch the octopus. I did not know it was angry," Tom said.

"Tom, you have to listen to your mom and dad. They know what is best for you. They want to keep you safe. You have to be careful and respectful of the animals. They have feelings too. They do not like to be bothered or hurt. Do you understand?" his dad said.

"Yes, dad. I understand. I will listen to you and mom. I will not touch the octopus or any other animal without your permission. I learned my lesson," Tom said.

The moral of the story is: Listen to your parents and respect the animals.

One day, a smart boy came and said he could break the rock. He tried and tried, but he couldn't do it. Then he had an idea. He used his cane to hit the rock and it broke into a million pieces! Everyone was so happy and the boy was a hero.

Joe was amazed by the story. He thanked Sam for telling him the story and hugged him goodbye. They both smiled and went home.

When Sam was finished swimming, he sat on an ordinary seat with his mommy. "That was so much fun," said Sam. His mommy smiled and said, "Yes, it was. You are an excellent swimmer!" 

Sam smiled and said, "Let's come back to the swimming pool again sometime soon!" Sam's mommy said, "Yes, I'd love to!" And so Sam and his mommy swam together often, to have even more fun.

Daisy was very relieved that the machine was working again and she was proud of her accomplishment. From then on, she knew to always be careful with the things that can be found in the big house.

"No, sweetie, you have to wait. It's a very special present, and you will love it. But you have to be patient and go to sleep first. Then you can open it in the morning, okay?" his mom said, as she tucked him in his bed.

"Okay, mom. I love you. Good night," Timmy said, as he gave her a kiss.

"I love you too, Timmy. Good night," his mom said, as she turned off the light and closed the door.

Timmy tried to sleep, but he was too curious and excited. He wondered what his present could be. Maybe it was a new bike, or a big teddy bear, or a cool robot. He imagined all the fun things he could do with his present. He smiled and closed his eyes.

But then he heard a strange noise. It sounded like a growl, or a roar, or a snarl. It came from the closet, where his mom and dad had hidden his present. Timmy felt fearful. He did not like the noise. He did not want to see his present anymore. He wanted his mom and dad to come and make the noise go away. He pulled the blanket over his head and hoped the noise would stop.

But it did not stop. It got louder and louder. Timmy heard the closet door open and something big and furry come out. He heard it walk towards his bed, and sniff his blanket. He heard it breathe and snort. He was too scared to scream or run. He just lay still and hoped it would not hurt him.

Then he felt something lick his face. He opened his eyes and saw a big, brown, fluffy dog. It wagged its tail and looked at him with friendly eyes. It was his present. His mom and dad had got him a puppy. Timmy was not fearful anymore. He was happy. He hugged the puppy and laughed.

"Hi, puppy. You're my present. You're my new friend. I love you," Timmy said, as he kissed the puppy.

The puppy barked and licked him back. It was happy too. It had a new home and a new friend. It loved Timmy.

"Surprise, Timmy. Happy birthday. We hope you like your present," his mom and dad said, as they came into the room with a big smile.

"I love it. Thank you, mom and dad. You're the best," Timmy said, as he showed them his puppy.

"You're welcome, Timmy. We're glad you like it. What are you going to name him?" his mom asked.

Timmy thought for a moment. Then he said, "I'm going to name him Yawn. Because he makes me yawn, and he yawns too. And because he's so cute and cuddly."

"Yawn. That's a perfect name for him. He's a sleepy puppy. Just like you. Now, why don't you and Yawn go to sleep? You have a big day tomorrow. You can play with him more in the morning," his dad said, as he tucked them in.

"Okay, dad. Good night, mom and dad. Good night, Yawn," Timmy said, as he snuggled with his puppy.

"Good night, Timmy. Good night, Yawn. We love you," his mom and dad said, as they turned off the light and closed the door.

Timmy and Yawn fell asleep, happy and warm. They dreamed of all the fun they would have together. They were the best present for each other.

Tom and Lily were twins who liked to sing and dance. They learned many songs and dances from their mom and dad, who were performers. Sometimes, they put on shows for their family and friends in their living room.

One day, they decided to perform a new song and dance for their mom and dad at dinner time. They practiced all afternoon, wearing their costumes and using their props. They were very excited and proud of their show.

When dinner time came, they set up their stage in the living room and asked their mom and dad to sit on the couch. They said, "We have a surprise for you! We are going to perform a new song and dance for you!"

Their mom and dad smiled and clapped their hands. They said, "We can't wait to see your show! You are such talented performers!"

Tom and Lily started their show. They sang a song about animals and danced like lions, monkeys, and elephants. They used their stuffed animals, hats, and scarves as props. They had a lot of fun and made their mom and dad laugh and cheer.

But then, something went wrong. Lily tripped over a scarf and fell down. She hurt her knee and started to cry. Tom stopped singing and dancing and ran to help her. He said, "Are you okay, Lily? I'm sorry you fell down."

Lily said, "It's okay, Tom. It's just a little scratch. But I'm sad we couldn't finish our show."

Their mom and dad got up from the couch and hugged them. They said, "Don't be sad, Lily and Tom. You did a great job! We loved your show! You are very brave and creative performers!"

Tom and Lily felt better and smiled. They said, "Thank you, mom and dad. We love you!"

Their mom and dad said, "We love you too! And we have another surprise for you. We made your favorite dinner: pizza and ice cream!"

Tom and Lily cheered and said, "Yay! Pizza and ice cream! That's the best dinner ever!"

They all went to the kitchen and enjoyed their dinner. They talked about their show and their animals. They were very happy and proud of themselves.

But their stuffed animals were confused. They didn't understand why Tom and Lily stopped singing and dancing. They wanted to see the end of the show. They waited on the stage, hoping that Tom and Lily would come back and perform for them.

Tom and Jen were twins. They liked to play and have fun. But they did not like to sleep. They said sleep was boring and scary. They had nightmares every night. They saw monsters and ghosts and spiders in their dreams.

One night, their mom said, "It's time for bed, Tom and Jen. You need to sleep well and have sweet dreams."

Tom and Jen said, "No, mom, we don't want to sleep. We want to stay up and play. Sleep is boring and scary. We have nightmares every night."

Mom said, "I know, my loves, but sleep is good for you. It helps you grow and learn and be happy. And you don't have to be afraid of nightmares. They are not real. They are just pictures in your head. You can make them go away by thinking of something nice, like your favorite toy or your best friend."

Tom and Jen said, "But mom, we can't. The nightmares are too strong. They make us cry and scream and sweat. We want to join you in your bed. Can we, mom, please?"

Mom said, "No, my loves, you can't. You have your own beds. You need to sleep in them. You are big kids now. You can do it. I will give you a kiss and a hug and a story. And I will leave the light on and the door open. And I will check on you later. OK?"

Tom and Jen said, "OK, mom, we will try. But we are still scared."

Mom said, "Don't be scared, my loves. I am here for you. I love you. Good night."

Mom gave them a kiss and a hug and a story. She left the light on and the door open. She went to her bed.

Tom and Jen lay in their beds. They closed their eyes. They tried to think of something nice. But they could not. They only saw nightmares. They saw monsters and ghosts and spiders in their dreams. They cried and screamed and sweat.

They wanted to join mom in her bed. They wanted to feel safe and warm. They got out of their beds. They ran to mom's room. They opened the door.

But mom was not there. She was gone. The bed was empty. The window was broken. There was blood on the floor. There was a note on the pillow. It said, "I have your mom. She is mine now. You can't join her. You can only join me. In your nightmares. Forever."

Tom and Jen screamed. They screamed and screamed and screamed. But no one heard them. No one came. No one helped. They were alone. They were trapped. They were doomed.

But when they got to the airport, they saw a lot of people and a lot of noise. Lily and Tom felt scared and confused. They did not like the airport. They wanted to go back home.

"Mom, Dad, can we go home?" Lily asked.

"But the airport is too big and too loud. I don't like it," Tom said.

"I know, honey, but it will be over soon. Look, there is a nice lady who will help us. She will check our bags and give us tickets. Let's say hello to her," Dad said.

Lily and Tom followed Mom and Dad to the nice lady. She smiled at them and asked them their names. She gave them stickers and tickets and told them they were brave. Lily and Tom felt a little better. They thanked the nice lady and followed Mom and Dad to the plane.

On the plane, Lily and Tom sat next to the window. They saw the airport get smaller and smaller as the plane went up. They saw the clouds and the sun and the birds. They felt happy and excited. They forgot about the airport.

"Look, Lily, we are flying!" Tom said.

"Yes, Tom, we are flying! We are going to see Grandma and Grandpa!" Lily said.

They hugged Mom and Dad and smiled. They managed to go to the airport and get on the plane. They learned that sometimes things can be scary and hard, but with the help of their parents and nice people, they can do it. They learned to be brave and curious. They learned to enjoy the adventure.

They reach the bottom of the hill. They see a man. The man has a big stick. The man sees the bear.

"Go away, bear!" the man says. He waves the stick.

The bear stops. The bear is afraid of the man. The bear runs away.

Lily and Tom are safe. They hug the man.

"Thank you, man!" they say.

"You're welcome, kids!" he says. "But don't climb that hill again. It's dangerous. There are bears there."

"We won't, man!" they say.

Lily liked to go to the zoo with her mom. She loved to see all the animals, but her favorite was the octopus. She liked how it had eight arms and could change colors. She wanted to be friends with the octopus.

One day, she asked her mom if she could go closer to the glass and say hello to the octopus. Her mom said yes, but told her to be careful and not touch the glass. Lily nodded and walked slowly to the tank. She saw the octopus hiding in a corner, looking shy.

"Hi, octopus," Lily said softly. "I like you. You are very pretty. Do you want to play with me?"

The octopus heard Lily's voice and peeked out of its hiding place. It saw Lily's smiling face and felt curious. It swam closer to the glass and looked at Lily with its big eyes.

"Hi, Lily," the octopus said in a low voice. "I like you too. You are very nice. But I am shy. I don't know how to play with you."

Lily thought for a moment. She wanted to make the octopus happy and not scared. She had an idea.

"How about we kiss?" she asked. "Kissing is a nice way to show that we are friends. You can kiss me with one of your arms, and I can kiss you with my lips. Do you want to try?"

The octopus felt shy, but also brave. It wanted to kiss Lily and show that it was a friend. It nodded and stretched one of its arms to the glass. Lily leaned forward and kissed the octopus's arm gently. The octopus felt a warm and soft touch on its skin. It liked it. It smiled and kissed Lily's lips with its mouth. Lily felt a wet and ticklish touch on her lips. She liked it too. She giggled and hugged the glass.

They kissed and smiled and played for a while. They were happy. They were friends.

"No, you can't!" he said. "This is my ice cream! Go away!"

He held his ice cream cone higher, away from the children.

Anna and Ben felt sad and angry. They thought the man was mean and selfish. They wanted to make him give them some ice cream.

"Hey, that's not fair!" Ben said. "You have so much ice cream! You should share with us!"

"Oh no!" the man said. "My ice cream! It's melting!"

He looked at his ice cream cone. It was almost gone. He felt sad and sorry. He wished he had shared his ice cream with the children.

One day, Anna and her mom went to the city. They saw many things, like cars, shops, and people. Anna liked the city, but she also wanted to see the big building where the opera singers sang. She asked her mom if they could go there, but her mom said no. She said opera was not for little girls, and it was too expensive and too late.

Anna was sad, but she did not say anything. She followed her mom as they walked around the city. But when they stopped at a crosswalk, Anna saw something. Across the street, there was a big sign that said "Opera Tonight". And next to the sign, there was a door that was open. Anna could hear music coming from the door. It was opera music.

Anna felt a tug in her heart. She wanted to hear more of the opera music. She wanted to see the opera singers. She did not want to wait for the green light. She let go of her mom's hand and ran across the street. She did not see the cars or the people. She only saw the door and the sign.

"Anna, stop!" her mom shouted. But Anna did not hear her. She reached the door and went inside. She wandered into a dark hallway, where the music was louder and clearer. She followed the music, until she came to a big room. It was the opera room. There were many seats, and many people, and a big stage. On the stage, there were opera singers. They wore pretty dresses and suits, and they sang with big voices. Anna was amazed. She had never seen anything like it.

She wanted to get closer. She wanted to see their faces and hear their words. She walked down the aisle, between the seats and the people. She did not care if they looked at her or whispered. She only cared about the opera. She reached the front row, and climbed over the railing. She stepped onto the stage, and walked towards the singers.

The singers did not see her. They were too busy singing and acting. They did not notice the little girl who wandered onto the stage, until it was too late. Anna walked right into the middle of the scene, and bumped into one of the singers. The singer stopped singing, and looked down at her. He was surprised and angry. She looked around, and saw her mom. Her mom was in the audience, and she looked worried and angry too. She called her name, "Anna, come here!"

Anna ran to her mom. She climbed over the railing, and jumped into her arms. Her mom hugged her, and scolded her, "Anna, what were you thinking? You could have been hurt! You could have caused an accident! You should never wander off like that!"

Anna felt sorry. She did not want to make her mom angry. She did not want to cause trouble. She only wanted to see the opera. She whispered, "I'm sorry, mom. I just wanted to sing."

Her mom sighed, and kissed her. She said, "I know, sweetie. I know you love to sing. But opera is not for little girls. Opera is for grown-ups. Maybe when you are older, you can see the opera. But for now, you have to listen to me, and stay with me, and be careful. OK?"

Anna nodded, and said, "OK, mom. I'm sorry. I love you."

Her mom smiled, and said, "I love you too, Anna. Now let's go home."

They left the opera room, and walked out of the door. They crossed the street, and took the bus. They went home, and had dinner. Anna did not sing that night. She was too tired, and too ashamed. She went to bed, and dreamed of opera.

But Sara did not feel happy. She felt lonely. She looked at the other dolls. They looked sad too. She wondered if she had made a mistake. She wondered if she should have shared Blue with Lily. She wondered if Lily would ever come back to play with her. She wondered if Blue was really her best friend.

Lily liked to bake with her mom. They made cakes and cookies and pies. Lily helped to mix and pour and decorate. She had a lot of fun.

One day, Lily saw a shiny metal pan on the table. It looked like a star. Lily wanted to bake something in it. She asked her mom, "Can we use this pan, please?"

Her mom said, "No, Lily, that pan is not for baking. It is for hanging on the wall. It is a decoration. It is very old and special. It was your grandma's pan. She gave it to me before she went to heaven."

Lily felt sad. She missed her grandma. She wanted to make her happy. She thought, maybe if she baked something in the pan, her grandma would see it and smile. She waited until her mom was busy. Then she took the pan and some dough and put them in the oven.

But the pan was not for baking. It was too thin and old. It got very hot and melted. The dough spilled and burned. The oven made a loud noise and smoke came out. Lily's mom ran to the kitchen and saw the mess. She was very angry and scared. She yelled at Lily, "What did you do? You could have started a fire! You could have hurt yourself! You ruined the pan!"

Lily started to cry. She did not mean to do anything bad. She just wanted to bake something for her grandma. She said, "I'm sorry, mom. I wanted to make you and grandma happy. I loved the pan. It was so pretty. I thought grandma would like it."

Her mom hugged her and said, "I'm sorry, too, Lily. I know you meant well. But you have to listen to me. The pan was not for baking. It was a gift from grandma. She loved it, too. She wanted us to keep it and remember her. Now it is gone. We are both sad."

They cleaned up the kitchen and threw away the pan. They looked at the pictures of grandma on the wall. They said, "We love you, grandma. We miss you."

They decided to bake something else. They used a different pan. They made a heart-shaped cake. They decorated it with icing and sprinkles. They ate it and shared it with their friends. They felt a little better. They still loved and missed grandma. But they also loved and enjoyed each other. They knew grandma would want them to be happy.

"Yes, he is. Do you know why?" mom asked.

"No, why?" Ben said.

"Because he lives in a place that is very cold sometimes. The hair helps him stay warm. But not all elephants are hairy. Some live in places that are very hot, and they have less hair," mom explained.

"Wow, that's cool!" Ben said.

"Can we feed the elephant, mom?" Lily asked.

"Sure, we can. See, there are some apples and carrots over there. We can buy some and give them to the elephant. But be careful, don't get too close to his mouth. He might think your hand is food, too," mom said.

Ben and Lily were surprised. They didn't know the elephant could talk.

"Bye, kids! I will remember you!" the elephant said.

Tom and Sam were brothers who liked to play on the farm. They had many animals to see and feed, like cows, pigs, chickens and horses. One day, they decided to explore the big barn where the hay was stored. Tom was older and braver than Sam, and he wanted to climb to the top of the hay pile.

"Come on, Sam, it will be fun!" Tom said. "We can see the whole farm from up there!"

Sam was scared and did not want to go. He saw how high the hay pile was and how dark the barn was. He thought there might be rats or spiders or snakes hiding in the hay.

"No, Tom, I don't want to go!" Sam said. "It is too high and too scary! Let's play somewhere else!"

But Tom did not listen to Sam. He insisted that Sam should follow him and be brave. He said that Sam was a baby and a chicken if he did not go. He made fun of Sam and hurt his feelings.

"Fine, be a baby then!" Tom said. "I will go by myself and have all the fun! You can stay here and cry!"

Tom ran to the hay pile and started to climb. Sam felt sad and angry and alone. He wished Tom would be nice to him and play with him. He did not like the barn at all.

Tom climbed higher and higher, until he reached the top of the hay pile. He felt proud and happy. He looked around and saw the farm and the sky and the sun. He shouted to Sam to look at him and see how cool he was.

"Hey, Sam, look at me!" Tom said. "I am the king of the barn! I am not afraid of anything!"

But Sam did not look at Tom. He did not hear Tom. He did not care about Tom. He was too busy running away from the barn, because he saw something that Tom did not see.

He saw a big fire.

The fire started from a spark that came from a broken wire. The spark lit the hay and the wood and the straw. The fire grew bigger and bigger, and it made a lot of smoke and noise. The fire was very hot and very dangerous.

Sam ran to the house and told his mom and dad about the fire. They called the firemen and tried to save the animals. They looked for Tom, but they could not find him. They shouted his name, but he did not answer. He was too busy screaming and crying and burning.

Tom was trapped on the hay pile. He could not climb down or jump off. He was surrounded by fire and smoke and flames. He was scared and hurt and sorry. He wished he had listened to Sam and played somewhere else. He wished he had been nice to Sam and not made fun of him. He wished he could say sorry to Sam and hug him.

But it was too late.

Tom died in the fire.

Sam was safe, but he was sad. He missed his brother and he blamed himself. He thought it was his fault that Tom died, because he did not go with him or help him. He felt guilty and lonely and ashamed.

He wished he could see Tom again and tell him he loved him.

But he could not.

The end.

"I don't know, sweetie," her mom replied.

Lily wanted to make the man feel better, so she went up to him and said, "Excuse me, sir. Would you like me to order you a bag of chips from the snack stand?"

The man looked up at her and smiled. "That's very kind of you, little girl. Thank you."

Lily ran to the snack stand and ordered a bag of chips for the man. When she brought it back to him, he thanked her and started to eat them. As Lily and her mom walked away, the man called out to them, "Thank you for making my day brighter!"

The moral of the story is that even small acts of kindness can make a big difference in someone's life.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a shiny red bicycle that she loved to ride every day. One day, while she was riding her bicycle, she saw a little bird that had fallen from its nest. The bird looked helpless and couldn't fly.

Lily stopped her bicycle and went to the bird. "What's your name, little bird?" she asked. The bird didn't answer, but Lily knew that it needed help. She picked up the bird and took it to her house.

Lily's mom helped her take care of the bird and they named it Tweety. They fed Tweety and kept it warm until it was strong enough to fly again. Lily was happy that she could help Tweety and learned that it's important to help others when they are helpless.

Lily's little brother Max was playing with his toys. Lily asked Max if she could play with him, but Max said no. Lily felt angry and wanted to yell, but she remembered her mom always said to use kind words. So, Lily said to Max, "Please can I play with you?"

Max said yes, and they played together for a long time. They built a tower with blocks, played with dolls, and even drew pictures. Lily was happy she didn't get angry and used kind words like her mom taught her.

In the end, Lily was glad she listened to her mom and stayed inside where it was cooler. She had a fun day playing with her little brother Max, and she learned that using kind words can make people happy.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl. She was three years old and loved going for walks. On this day, she was feeling very brave, so she decided to march all the way to the park by herself. As she marched along, she saw lots of interesting things. She saw birds flying in the sky, butterflies flitting around the flowers, a squirrel scurrying up a tree and a bright rainbow above her. 

At last, she reached the park. It was so beautiful! There was a babbling stream and the grass was so green and soft. The little girl felt calm as she watched the sun glistening through the trees. Suddenly, from behind her, she heard a voice. It was an old lady, wearing a veil. She smiled at the little girl.

"I see you marching around. You must be very brave!" She said.

The little girl nodded and smiled back. They both stood in silence for a while, enjoying the beauty of the park and the peace of being together. Then, the old lady offered to share her veil with the little girl. She said it was made of the brightest stars. The little girl put it on and suddenly the park was even more magical. 

The little girl thanked the old lady and marched back home, wearing the starry veil. All around her was calmness and beauty and the little girl felt so happy.

Ben was a bunny who loved to hop. He hopped all over the meadow, looking for nuts to eat. He liked nuts very much. They were tasty and crunchy.

One day, he saw a big, shiny nut on a tree. It was the most attractive nut he had ever seen. He wanted it very much. He hopped closer to the tree and said, "Hello, nut. You are so pretty. Can I have you?"

The nut did not answer. It was not a real nut. It was a trap. A hunter had put it there to catch bunnies. He was hiding behind a bush, waiting for Ben to come closer.

Ben did not know that. He hopped closer and closer to the nut. He reached out his paw to touch it. But before he could, he heard a loud snap. A metal ring closed around his neck. He was caught. He felt scared and sad.

"Help! Help!" he cried. "Let me go!"

The hunter came out of his hiding place. He smiled and said, "Gotcha, you silly bunny. You fell for my trick. You should not be so greedy and foolish. You should be happy with what you have."

He picked up Ben and put him in a cage. He took him away from the meadow. Ben never saw his home or his friends again.

The moral of the story is: Do not be greedy and foolish. Be happy with what you have.

Tom did not listen. He ran away with the cane. He laughed and waved it in the air. He did not see the big dog. The big dog was angry. It barked and chased Tom. Tom was scared. He dropped the cane and tried to run. But it was too late. The big dog bit Tom on the leg. Tom cried and screamed. He was hurt and sorry.

The old man heard Tom. He picked up his cane and walked to him. He saw the blood and the bite. He felt sorry for Tom. He said, "You should not touch things that are not yours. You should say sorry and ask first. Now you are in trouble. Where is your mom?"

Tom did not answer. He was too sad and ashamed. He wished he had not touched the cane. He wished he had been a good boy.

Sara and Ben were playing in the field. They liked to run and jump and pick flowers. They saw a big tree with red apples. Sara wanted to eat an apple, but she was too small to reach them.

"Ben, can you help me get an apple?" Sara asked.

"OK, Sara. I will try. You wait here and be patient," Ben said. He climbed the tree and looked for a good apple. He found one and pulled it hard. But the apple was too big and heavy. It fell on Ben's head and made him cry.

"Ow, ow, ow! That hurts!" Ben shouted.

Sara heard Ben's cry and ran to the tree. She saw Ben on the ground with a big bump on his head. She felt sorry for him and hugged him.

"Ben, are you OK? I'm sorry you got hurt. Here, have this apple. It's for you," Sara said. She gave him the apple that fell on his head.

Ben smiled and took the apple. He thanked Sara and gave her a kiss. He felt better and stopped crying.

"Thank you, Sara. You are a good friend. Do you want to share this apple with me?" Ben asked.

"Yes, Ben. I would like that. You are a good friend, too. Let's eat this apple and then play some more," Sara said.

They ate the apple and then played some more in the field. They were happy and forgot about the bump. They had fun until it was time to go home.

Sara and Tom were playing on the beach. They liked to find shells and make patterns in the sand. Sara found a big shell that was shiny and pink. She was very happy and showed it to Tom.

"Wow, that is a pretty shell!" Tom said. "Can I see it?"

Sara nodded and gave him the shell. Tom looked at it and smiled. He liked it too. He wanted to keep it for himself. He had an idea.

"Hey, Sara, do you want to see something cool?" he asked. "Follow me, I will lead you to a secret place."

Sara was curious and followed Tom. Tom led her to a big rock that was far from the water. He told her to look behind the rock. There was nothing there.

"Where is the cool thing?" Sara asked.

Tom did not answer. He ran away with the shell. He was not honest. He lied to Sara and took her shell.

Sara was sad and angry. She cried and looked for Tom. She saw him hiding behind a palm tree. She ran to him and shouted.

"Tom, give me back my shell! You are not nice! You are not my friend!"

Tom felt bad. He saw that Sara was hurt. He realized that he was wrong. He was sorry.

"Sara, I am sorry. I was selfish. I lied to you and took your shell. Here, take it back. It is yours. You are nice. You are my friend."

Sara stopped crying. She took the shell and looked at Tom. She saw that he was honest. He said sorry and gave her back the shell. She forgave him.

"Tom, thank you. I am glad you are sorry. I forgive you. You are nice. You are my friend."

Sara and Tom hugged and smiled. They learned a lesson. They learned to be honest and share. They learned to be good friends. They went back to the beach and played with the shells. They were happy.

Tom and Lily were twins who liked to play together. One day, they decided to make soup for their mom, who was sick in bed. They took a big pot and filled it with water, carrots, potatoes, and salt. They put the pot on the stove and turned it on.

"Mom will love our soup!" Tom said.

"Yes, she will!" Lily said. "But we have to wait for it to boil."

They sat on the floor and played with their toys while the soup cooked. They were very quiet, so they would not disturb their mom.

But then, they heard a loud noise from the stove. They looked up and saw that the soup was bubbling over and making a mess.

"Oh no!" Tom and Lily cried. "The soup is too hot!"

They ran to the stove and tried to turn it off. But they were too small and could not reach the knob. They started to cry and call for their mom.

Mom heard their cries and got out of bed. She saw the soup spilling over and the twins crying. She quickly turned off the stove and cleaned up the mess. She hugged Tom and Lily and thanked them for their soup.

"I'm sorry, Mom," Tom said. "We wanted to make you soup, but we made a mess."

"It's okay, Tom," Mom said. "It was very sweet of you to try. But next time, you have to ask me before you use the stove. It can be very dangerous."

"I'm sorry, Mom," Lily said. "We didn't mean to disturb you. We wanted to make you happy."

"It's okay, Lily," Mom said. "You did make me happy. You are very kind and thoughtful. But next time, you have to be careful and listen to me. I know what is best for you."

Mom took the pot of soup and poured some into a bowl. She tasted it and smiled.

"Your soup is very good," Mom said. "You did a great job. Do you want some?"

"Yes, please!" Tom and Lily said.

Mom gave them each a bowl of soup and a spoon. They sat on the couch and ate their soup with Mom. They felt warm and cozy.

"Mom, we love you," Tom and Lily said.

"I love you too, my fair twins," Mom said.

But the rabbit is too fast for Lily. It runs away and hides in a hole. Lily can't see the rabbit anymore. She is sad. She says, "Where is the rabbit? I want to number the rabbit."

Her mom comes to her and hugs her. She says, "Don't be sad, Lily. The rabbit is shy. It doesn't like to be numbered. It likes to be free. Why don't you number something else? Look, there are some flowers on the grass. They are pretty and colorful. Do you want to number the flowers?"

Lily smiles and nods. She says, "Yes, I want to number the flowers. They are nice and smell good." She goes to the flowers and starts to number them. She says, "One, two, three, four, five..." She is happy again. She likes to number things.

"Be careful, Ben," Anna says. "The thorns can hurt you."

Ben nods, but he is curious. He reaches for a flower, but he pricks his finger. He cries out in pain.

Anna hears him and runs to him. She sees his finger and feels sorry for him.

"Don't cry, Ben," she says. "I will help you."

Anna smiles too. She is happy to help her brother.

Anna was scared. She had a bad dream. A big monster chased her in the dark. She woke up and cried. She wanted her mom.

Mom heard Anna cry. She ran to her room. She hugged Anna and said, "It's okay, sweetie. You had a nightmare. A nightmare is a bad dream that makes you feel scared. But it's not real. It's only in your head."

Anna sniffled and said, "But the monster was so big and mean. It wanted to eat me."

Mom said, "I know, honey. But the monster can't hurt you. It's gone now. You are safe with me. I love you very much. Do you want me to explain how to make the nightmares go away?"

Anna nodded. She wanted to feel better.

Mom said, "Okay, listen. When you have a nightmare, you can do three things. One, you can tell yourself that it's not real and that you are brave. Two, you can think of something happy and nice, like your favorite toy or your best friend. Three, you can ask me or dad to come and cuddle you and sing you a song. Do you think you can do that?"

Anna said, "Yes, mom. I can do that. Thank you for explaining. Can you cuddle me and sing me a song now?"

Mom said, "Of course, my love. Let's cuddle and sing. And then you can sleep again. And have sweet dreams."

Lila was a proud girl who liked to wear her red dress and her shiny shoes. She wanted to show them to her friend Max, who lived next door. She ran to his house and knocked on the door.

"Hi, Lila!" Max said, opening the door. "Do you want to play with me?"

"Yes, please!" Lila said. "Look at my dress and my shoes. Aren't they pretty?"

"They are very pretty," Max said. "But do you want to see something even prettier?"

"What is it?" Lila asked, curious.

Max led her to his backyard, where he had a big cage with a colorful parrot inside. The parrot had feathers of blue, green, yellow and red. It looked at Lila and Max with bright eyes.

"Wow!" Lila said. "What is his name?"

"His name is Coco," Max said. "He can talk, too. Watch this. Coco, say hello to Lila."

"Hello, Lila!" Coco said, in a clear voice.

"Hello, Coco!" Lila said, amazed. "You are a smart parrot!"

"Thank you, thank you!" Coco said, flapping his wings.

Lila and Max laughed and clapped. They decided to play with Coco for a while. They taught him some new words, like "banana" and "flower". Coco repeated them happily.

But then, Lila got too excited and wanted to touch Coco. She reached out her hand to the cage, but she stumbled on a rock and fell down. She scraped her knee and started to cry.

"Ouch, ouch!" Coco said, copying her.

Lila felt a sharp pain in her knee and a tear in her dress. She looked at her shoes and saw that they were dirty. She felt sad and angry.

"Bad parrot!" she shouted at Coco. "You made me fall!"

"No, no!" Coco said. "I didn't do anything!"

Max ran to Lila and helped her up. He saw that she was hurt and he felt sorry for her.

"Lila, are you okay?" he asked. "I'm sorry you fell. It was an accident. Coco didn't mean to make you fall. He was just talking to you."

Lila sniffed and wiped her tears. She looked at Coco and saw that he looked scared and sad, too. He hid in a corner of the cage and said nothing.

Lila realized that she was wrong to blame Coco. He was a nice parrot who wanted to be her friend. She felt sorry for him, too.

"Lila, do you want to say sorry to Coco?" Max asked. "He might feel better if you do."

Lila nodded and walked to the cage. She smiled at Coco and said:

"I'm sorry, Coco. You are a good parrot. I like you."

Coco peeked out of the corner and smiled back. He said:

"I'm sorry, Lila. You are a nice girl. I like you, too."

Lila and Coco hugged through the bars of the cage. Max smiled and hugged them both. They were all happy again.

The End.

Tim and Kim decided to ask the boy if they could trade their big ball for his small ball. The boy agreed. He gave them his small ball and took their big ball. He thanked them and left.

Tim and Kim played with the small ball. They threw it to each other and caught it. They threw it at targets and hit them. They had fun with their ball. They learned that bigger is not always better. Sometimes, smaller is more fun. They had success with their ball. They were happy.

Lily and Ben are friends who like to swim in the sea. They wear masks and fins to see the fish and the reef. The reef is a big rock with many colors and shapes under the water. Lily and Ben like to look for shells and starfish on the reef.

One day, they see a big boat near the reef. The boat is making a lot of noise and smoke. Lily and Ben are curious and swim closer to the boat. They see a man on the boat who is holding a big tube. The man puts the tube in the water and pushes a button. The tube makes a loud boom and a lot of bubbles.

Lily and Ben are scared and swim away from the boat. They see that the reef is hurt by the boom. Some parts of the reef are broken and some fish are floating. The water is dirty and cloudy. Lily and Ben are sad and angry.

"Hey, you!" Lily shouts at the man on the boat. "What are you doing? You are hurting the reef and the fish!"

The man looks at Lily and Ben and says, "I am testing the water. I need to see how deep and how hard the reef is. It is my job."

"But you are making the water dirty and the reef sick!" Ben says. "The reef is not yours to test. It is home for the fish and for us. You should stop and go away!"

The man shrugs and says, "I don't care. I have to do what I have to do. You kids should mind your own business and leave me alone."

Lily and Ben are very upset. They swim back to the shore and tell their parents what they saw. Their parents are also upset and call the police. The police come and talk to the man on the boat. They tell him that he is breaking the law and that he has to stop testing the reef. They also tell him that he has to pay for the damage he caused to the reef and the fish.

Lily and Ben are happy that the police help them. They hope that the reef will heal and that the fish will come back. They promise to take care of the reef and to protect it from bad people. They hug each other and say, "We are friends of the reef!"

Anna and Ben were twins who loved to play with their toys. They had many toys, but their favorite was a big dollhouse that their grandma gave them. The dollhouse had many rooms, furniture, and dolls. It was a luxury that made them very happy.

Jen disagrees. She says, "This wire is dull. It is not a toy. It can hurt us. Look, it has a sharp end. It can cut us. We should leave it alone."

Lily and Ben were twins who liked to play together. One day, they found a banana in the kitchen. They decided to share it, but they did not know how to peel it. It was difficult.

"Let me do it," said Lily. She tried to pull the skin, but it was too hard. She hurt her finger and cried.

"No, let me do it," said Ben. He tried to bite the skin, but it was too tough. He hurt his teeth and cried.

They both wanted the banana, but they could not open it. They were sad and angry.

"We want to eat the banana, but we can't peel it. It's difficult," said Lily and Ben.

Mom hugged them and said, "Don't worry, I can help you. But first, you have to say sorry to each other. You should not fight over the banana. You should share and help each other."

Lily and Ben felt sorry and said, "Sorry, Lily. Sorry, Ben. We love you."

They cried and shouted, "Help, mom, help! We are sorry, mom, we are sorry! We will give away some of our things and clean our room. Please, mom, please!"

Mom heard them and came to their room. She opened the door and saw them covered in dust. She said, "Tim and Kim, I told you what would happen if you did not listen. This is what you get for being greedy and lazy. But I still love you and I will help you. Come, let's go to the bathroom and wash up. Then we will sort out your things and give some away. And then we will clean your room and make it nice and neat."

Tim and Kim nodded and hugged their mom. They said, "Thank you, mom, thank you. We love you, mom, we love you. We learned our lesson, mom, we learned our lesson. We will not be greedy and lazy anymore. We will share and tidy up."

Mom smiled and said, "That's good, Tim and Kim, that's good. I am proud of you, Tim and Kim, I am proud of you. Now let's go and do what we have to do."

The end.

Tom and Lily were friends who liked to play outside. They had a big box of chalk and they used it to draw on the sidewalk. They drew flowers, stars, animals and letters. They had a lot of fun.

One day, they saw a big cake in the window of a bakery. It looked delicious. It had white cream, red cherries and chocolate sprinkles. Tom and Lily wanted to eat the cake. They had no money, but they had an idea.

They took their chalk and drew a big circle on the sidewalk. Then they lay down inside the circle and pretended to be asleep. They hoped that someone would see them and feel sorry for them and give them some cake.

A kind lady walked by and saw Tom and Lily. She thought they were poor and hungry. She went into the bakery and bought a slice of cake for each of them. She came out and put the cake next to them. She said, "Wake up, children. I have a treat for you. You must be very hungry."

Tom and Lily opened their eyes and saw the cake. They were very happy. They thanked the lady and ate the cake. It was delicious. They smiled at each other.

But then they felt bad. They knew they had lied to the lady. They had not been hungry. They had just been greedy. They had used their chalk to trick her. They felt sorry for what they had done.

They decided to tell the lady the truth. They ran after her and said, "Lady, we are sorry. We lied to you. We were not hungry. We just wanted the cake. We have a home and a family and food. We have chalk and we like to draw. We are sorry for being bad."

The lady was surprised and angry. She said, "How could you do that? You should not lie to people. You should not take what is not yours. You should be grateful for what you have. You should be honest and kind. You should say sorry and give back the cake."

Tom and Lily felt ashamed. They said sorry and gave back the cake. They said they would never lie again. They said they would share their chalk with other children who had none. They said they would be good friends.

The lady forgave them and hugged them. She said, "I am glad you told me the truth. I hope you learned your lesson. You have a good heart. You can keep the cake. But remember, cake is not as delicious as honesty."

On Tuesday, Ben and his mom went to the park. Ben liked the park. He liked to slide, swing, and run. He also liked to whistle. He learned to whistle from his dad. He whistled loud and happy.

At the park, Ben saw a bird. The bird was red and black. It was on a branch. The bird whistled too. It whistled soft and pretty. Ben wanted to talk to the bird. He whistled back. The bird looked at him.

Ben and the bird whistled to each other. They made a song. Ben's mom smiled. She liked the song. She took a picture of Ben and the bird. She said, "You are very good at whistling, Ben. You made a new friend."

Ben was happy. He liked his new friend. He said, "Thank you, bird. You are very good at whistling too. You made me happy." The bird nodded. It flew away. Ben waved. He said, "Bye, bird. See you next Tuesday."

Ben and his mom went home. Ben was ready for a nap. He dreamed of the bird and the song. He whistled in his sleep.

They got in the car and drove to the airport. The airport was very busy and noisy. There were many people and bags and carts. Tom and Lily held their mom and dad's hands and followed them to the check-in counter. They gave their bags to a lady who put them on a belt. Then they got their tickets and went to the security gate.

But when they got to the other side, they saw that their mom and dad were not there. They had gone to another line and were waiting for them. Tom and Lily felt scared and started to cry. They missed their mom and dad.

"Mom! Dad! Where are you?" they shouted.

A nice man in a uniform heard them and came to help. He asked them their names and looked at their tickets. He said he would take them to their mom and dad. He picked up their backpacks and coats and held their hands. He walked with them through the crowd and found their mom and dad. They were so happy to see them and hugged them tight.

"Sorry, kids, we didn't see you. Are you OK?" their mom asked.

"Yes, we're OK. But we missed you," Lily said.

"Thank you, sir, for helping us," their dad said to the nice man.

"You're welcome. Have a nice flight," the nice man said and smiled.

"Look, I made a flower!" Lily says, showing Tom her pink and yellow magnets.

"That's nice, Lily. Can I take this blue magnet?" Tom asks, pointing to a round magnet.

"OK, you can take it. But don't take my green magnet. It's my favorite," Lily says.

Tom takes the blue magnet and puts it next to his red magnet. He tries to make a car. But the magnets don't stick together. They push each other away.

"Why don't they stick?" Tom asks, confused.

"Because they are not friends. They are opposite. Like wet and dry," Lily explains.

"Oh, I see. Wet and dry are opposite. Like hot and cold," Tom says.

"Yes, like hot and cold. And like big and small," Lily says.

They look at each other and smile. They are not opposite. They are friends. They hug and keep playing with magnets.

Lily liked to write in her journal every day. She wrote about her friends, her toys, her dreams, and her feelings. She used a red pen and drew pictures too. She kept her journal under her pillow, so no one could see it.

One day, she came home from school and saw her brother Jake in her room. He was holding her journal and laughing. He had read her secret words and seen her drawings. He saw that she had written "I love Tom" and drawn a heart with a kiss.

"Ha ha, Lily loves Tom! Lily loves Tom!" Jake teased her. He waved her journal in the air and ran away.

Lily felt angry and sad. She chased after Jake and tried to get her journal back. She shouted, "Give it back! Give it back! It's mine!"

Jake ran downstairs and into the living room. He saw Mom and Dad on the couch. He said, "Look, Mom and Dad, Lily loves Tom! She wrote it in her journal! She wants to kiss him!"

Mom and Dad looked surprised and confused. They did not know who Tom was. They did not know Lily had a journal. They did not know what to say.

Lily ran into the living room and snatched her journal from Jake. She hugged it to her chest and glared at him. She said, "You're mean! You're a bad brother! You don't read my journal! It's private!"

Mom and Dad tried to calm them down. They said, "Lily, Jake, stop fighting. We're sorry, Lily, we didn't know you had a journal. It's very normal to have feelings for someone. But you should also respect each other's privacy. Jake, you shouldn't have taken Lily's journal and made fun of her. That was not nice. You should apologize to her."

Jake felt sorry for what he had done. He said, "I'm sorry, Lily. I was just joking. I didn't mean to hurt you. I won't read your journal again. Can I see your drawings? They're pretty."

Lily felt a little better. She said, "It's okay, Jake. I forgive you. But don't tell anyone about Tom. He's my friend. Maybe I'll kiss him someday. Maybe not. It's my choice."

Mom and Dad smiled and hugged them. They said, "We're proud of you, Lily and Jake. You're growing up. You're learning to express yourselves and to be kind to each other. We love you both very much."

Lily and Jake hugged them back. They said, "We love you too, Mom and Dad."

They all sat on the couch and looked at Lily's journal together. They laughed and talked and shared their stories. They felt happy and normal.

One day, Lily was playing with Rose in her room. She pretended that Rose was her best friend and they were having a tea party. She talked to Rose with her hands, because she could not hear words. She gave Rose a cup of tea and a cookie, and said, "You are my best friend, Rose. I like you very much."

Rose did not answer, because she was a doll. But Lily did not mind. She smiled and hugged Rose. She felt happy.

Then, Lily heard a knock on the door. It was her brother, Tom. Tom was not deaf, he could hear words. He opened the door and saw Lily and Rose.

"Hi, Lily," he said. "Can I play with you?"

Lily looked at Tom and nodded. She liked Tom, he was nice to her. She moved over and made some space for him on the floor.

"This is my doll, Rose," she said to Tom with her hands. "She is my best friend."

Tom looked at Rose and smiled. He thought she was a pretty doll. He picked her up and said, "Hello, Rose. I am Tom. Nice to meet you."

But then, he noticed something. Rose had a hole in her leg. It was a big hole, and some stuffing was coming out.

"Oh, no," he said. "Rose has a hole in her leg. She is hurt. We need to fix her."

Lily saw the hole and felt sad. She did not know how Rose got the hole. She loved Rose and did not want her to be hurt. She said to Tom with her hands, "Can you help me fix her?"

Tom nodded. He was good at fixing things. He said, "Don't worry, Lily. I have some thread and a needle. I can sew the hole and make Rose better."

He went to his room and came back with the thread and the needle. He sat down next to Lily and Rose, and started to sew the hole. He was careful and gentle. He did not want to hurt Rose.

Lily watched him and felt grateful. She said to Tom with her hands, "Thank you, Tom. You are a good brother."

Tom smiled and said, "You're welcome, Lily. You are a good sister."

He finished sewing the hole and gave Rose back to Lily. He said, "There, she is fixed. She looks good as new."

Lily hugged Rose and felt happy. She looked at Tom and said with her hands, "You are my best friend, too, Tom. I like you very much."

Tom hugged Lily and said, "You are my best friend, too, Lily. I like you very much."

They smiled and played with Rose. They had a tea party and a cookie. They felt happy.

"Please let us get closer," Lucy asked her parents, who nodded with a smile. The bird flew around the plane, singing sweetly. He motioned for them with his wings, and the trio could hear him say, "C'mon up here. I'll show you all around!"

The bird took Lucy and her parents on a magical ride through the sky. He showed them things they had never seen before: twinkling star noise, a rare double rainbow and a forest of music. When it was time to go, the bird waved goodbye and said, "Please come back soon!"

Happy and exhausted, Lucy, smiled wide and said, "Today was one of the best days ever. Now I know just why the bird is so rare and special!"

One day, Tim sees a new truck in the street. It is yellow and shiny. It has a loud horn and a long trailer. Tim wants to play with it. He says to Ben, "Look at that truck! It is so cool! Let's try to get in it!"

Ben is scared. He says, "No, Tim! That is not our truck! That is someone else's truck! They will be angry if we touch it!"

But Tim does not listen. He runs to the yellow truck. He climbs on the trailer. He jumps to the cab. He opens the door. He sits on the seat. He feels uncomfortable. The seat is too big and hard. The wheel is too high and heavy. The buttons are too many and confusing.

He tries to honk the horn. He pushes a button. But it is not the horn. It is the engine. The truck starts to move. Tim is shocked. He does not know how to stop it. He screams for help.

Ben hears Tim. He runs after the truck. He shouts, "Tim, Tim, get out of the truck! You are in trouble!"

But it is too late. The truck is going too fast. It hits a car. It hits a tree. It hits a fence. It makes a big crash. Tim is hurt. He cries. He is sorry.

The owner of the truck comes out. He is angry. He sees Tim. He sees the damage. He calls the police. He says, "Who are you? What have you done? You are a bad boy!"

Tim is scared. He wishes he had listened to Ben. He wishes he had played with his own truck. He learns a lesson. He never tries to get in someone else's truck again.

Tim and Lily were playing in the park. They liked to pretend they were heroes who saved the world from bad guys. Tim had a cape and a mask. Lily had a hat and a sword.

"Look, there is a big monster!" Tim said, pointing to a tree. "We have to stop it before it eats the people!"

"OK, let's go!" Lily said, following Tim. They ran towards the tree, making loud noises and waving their toys.

But when they got closer, they saw that the tree was not a monster. It was a man. He was sitting under the tree, reading a book. He had a long beard and a big backpack. He looked at them with a smile.

"Hello, little heroes," he said. "What are you doing?"

Tim and Lily stopped. They felt shy and scared. They did not know the man. He was unknown to them.

"Who are you?" Tim asked. He used his question word.

"I'm a traveler," the man said. "I like to go to different places and learn new things. What are you doing?"

"We are playing," Lily said. "We are heroes who save the world."

"That's wonderful," the man said. "Do you want to hear a story about a real hero?"

Tim and Lily nodded. They liked stories. They sat down next to the man. He opened his book and began to read.

The story was about a girl who helped her village by planting trees and flowers. She was brave and kind. She made the world more beautiful.

Tim and Lily listened to the story. They liked the girl. They wanted to be like her.

"Wow, she is a great hero," Tim said.

"Yes, she is," the man said. "And do you know what? You can be heroes too. You don't need a cape or a mask or a hat or a sword. You just need to care about the world and the people in it. You can do small things that make a big difference. Like picking up trash, or sharing your toys, or saying thank you."

Tim and Lily thought about what the man said. They realized he was right. They wanted to do good things. They wanted to be heroes.

"Thank you for the story," Lily said.

"You're welcome," the man said. "And thank you for playing with me."

They hugged the man and said goodbye. They ran back to their parents, who were waiting for them. They told them about the man and the story. They said they learned something new.

They learned that heroes are not only in books. They are everywhere. And they can be anyone. Even unknown people.

Sam and Ben are brothers. They like to play with cars. They have many cars of different colors and sizes. They make zoom sounds when they move the cars on the floor.

One day, Sam finds a new car in his toy box. It is big and red and shiny. He is very happy. He wants to show it to Ben. He says, "Look, Ben, I have a new car. It is the best car ever. It can zoom very fast."

Ben looks at the car. He likes it too. He wants to play with it. He says, "Can I have a turn, Sam? Please, let me try your car. It looks so fun."

Sam shakes his head. He does not want to share. He says, "No, Ben, this is my car. You have your own cars. Go away."

Ben feels sad and angry. He tries to grab the car from Sam. Sam holds the car tight. They start to fight. They pull and push and shout.

Mom hears the noise. She comes to see what is wrong. She sees Sam and Ben fighting over the car. She is not happy. She says, "Stop, boys, stop. Fighting is not nice. You have to share your toys. Why are you so mean to each other?"

Sam and Ben stop fighting. They look at Mom. They feel sorry. They say, "Sorry, Mom. We are sorry."

Mom picks up the car. She says, "This is a nice car. But it is not worth fighting over. How about you take turns playing with it? Sam can play with it for ten minutes, then Ben can play with it for ten minutes. Is that fair?"

Sam and Ben nod. They agree. They say, "Yes, Mom. That is fair. Thank you, Mom."

Mom gives the car to Sam. She says, "Here, Sam, you can play with it first. But remember, when the time is up, you have to give it to Ben. OK?"

Sam says, "OK, Mom. Thank you, Mom." He takes the car and starts to zoom it on the floor. He smiles.

Ben watches Sam. He waits for his turn. He sees a hairy cat on the couch. He goes to pet the cat. The cat purrs. Ben smiles.

Mom watches Sam and Ben. She is glad they are not fighting anymore. She smiles.

Tim and Kim were twins who liked to play on the beach. One day, they found a big, shiny oyster on the sand. They wanted to open it and see what was inside.

"Maybe there is a pearl!" Tim said.

"Or a treasure!" Kim said.

They tried to pry the oyster open with their fingers, but it was too hard. They looked around for something to help them.

They saw a big rock nearby. Tim had an idea.

"Let's use the rock to smash the oyster!" he said.

He picked up the rock and raised it over his head. He was about to hit the oyster when he heard a voice.

"Pause, Tim! Pause, Kim!" the voice said.

They turned around and saw their mom. She looked worried.

"What are you doing, children?" she asked.

"We want to open the oyster, mom!" Tim said.

"We think there is something inside, mom!" Kim said.

Mom shook her head.

"That is not a good idea, children," she said. "The oyster is alive. It is a living thing, like you and me. It has a shell to protect itself. If you smash it, you will hurt it and make it die. That is not nice. That is not kind."

Tim and Kim looked at the oyster. They felt sorry for it. They did not want to hurt it or make it die.

They put down the rock and gently placed the oyster back on the sand.

"We are sorry, oyster," they said. "We did not know you were alive. We hope you are happy and safe."

Mom smiled and hugged them.

"I am proud of you, children," she said. "You are obedient and good. You listened to me and learned something new. You showed respect and kindness to the oyster. That is a very valuable thing. That is a treasure."

Tim and Kim smiled and hugged mom back.

They learned that the oyster was a living thing, and that living things deserve care and love. They learned that the best treasure is not something shiny or sparkly, but something that comes from the heart.

Tim and Jen were twins who liked to play together. One day, they saw a big package outside their door. It was wrapped in shiny paper and had a bow on top.

"Wow, what is that?" Tim asked.

"Maybe it is a present for us!" Jen said.

They ran to the package and tried to lift it, but it was too heavy. They looked for a tag, but there was none.

"Who sent it?" Tim wondered.

"Let's ask Mom," Jen suggested.

They ran inside and found Mom in the kitchen. She was making cookies and had flour on her face.

"Mom, Mom, there is a big package outside!" Tim said.

"A package? For who?" Mom asked.

"We don't know. There is no tag. Can we open it?" Jen said.

Mom smiled and wiped her face. "Oh, that package is for your grandma. She is coming to visit us tomorrow. She sent it ahead of time."

"Grandma is coming?" Tim and Jen said together.

"Yes, she is. She is very excited to see you. She told me on the phone. She also mentioned that she has a surprise for you in the package," Mom said.

"A surprise? What is it?" Tim and Jen asked.

Mom winked. "You'll have to wait and see. But I'll give you a hint. It is something soft and chubby and likes to cuddle."

Tim and Jen thought hard. What could it be? A pillow? A teddy bear? A puppy?

They decided to go back outside and look at the package again. Maybe they could hear something inside. They put their ears to the paper and listened.

They heard a faint meow.

Tim and Jen gasped. They looked at each other and smiled.

They knew what the surprise was. Grandma had sent them a kitten!

"What is an ambulance?" Anna asked.

"Why do you need an ambulance?" Ben asked.

"Because I hit your ball and it might have a hole. I want to reveal it to you and see if it can be fixed. I also want to make sure you are okay and say sorry again. You are very good kids and I don't want you to be sad or scared." the driver said.

"Hello, we are here to help. What happened?" one of them asked.

Lily liked yogurt very much. She ate it every morning with her spoon. She liked all kinds of yogurt: red, yellow, green, white. But her favorite was pink yogurt. It was sweet and light and made her happy.

One day, Mom gave Lily a bowl of blue yogurt. Lily looked at it and frowned. She did not want blue yogurt. She wanted pink yogurt.

"Mom, I don't like this yogurt," she said. "It is not pink. It is blue. Blue is for the sky, not for yogurt."

Mom smiled and said, "Lily, this is a special yogurt. It is blueberry yogurt. It has little blue fruits inside. They are good for you. They make you strong and smart. Why don't you try it?"

Lily shook her head. She did not want to try it. She pushed the bowl away. She complained, "No, Mom, I don't want blueberry yogurt. I want pink yogurt. Pink yogurt is the best. Please give me pink yogurt."

Mom sighed and said, "Lily, you are being very picky. You should not complain about your food. There are many children who have no yogurt at all. You should be grateful for what you have. And you should try new things. You might like them. Blueberry yogurt is very yummy. I like it very much. Here, I will show you."

Mom took a spoonful of blueberry yogurt and put it in her mouth. She made a happy sound and said, "Mmm, this is delicious. See, Lily, it is not bad. It is very good. Do you want to taste it?"

Lily looked at Mom. She saw that Mom was not lying. She saw that Mom was enjoying the blueberry yogurt. She felt curious. Maybe blueberry yogurt was not so bad. Maybe it was good. Maybe she would like it.

She reached for the spoon and said, "OK, Mom, I will try it. But only a little bit."

Mom gave her the spoon and said, "That's my girl. I am proud of you. Here you go. Try it and tell me what you think."

Lily took the spoon and put it in her mouth. She felt the little blue fruits burst on her tongue. She felt the sweet and light yogurt slide down her throat. She closed her eyes and smiled. She liked it. She liked it very much.

She opened her eyes and said, "Mom, you were right. This is yummy. I like blueberry yogurt. Can I have more?"

Mom hugged her and said, "Of course you can, Lily. I am glad you like it. You are a good girl. You tried something new and you liked it. That is wonderful. You can have blueberry yogurt today and pink yogurt tomorrow. How does that sound?"

Lily nodded and said, "That sounds good, Mom. Thank you for the blueberry yogurt. I love you."

Mom kissed her and said, "I love you too, Lily. You are my sweet and light girl."

Lila was a little girl who liked to dream. Every night, she closed her eyes and saw wonderful things. She dreamed of flying in the sky, swimming in the sea, and playing with animals. She loved animals, especially goats. She wished she had a goat of her own.

One night, she dreamed that she was in a farm. She saw a big barn, a green field, and many animals. She ran to the barn and found a goat. The goat was white and fluffy, with horns and a beard. It looked at her with friendly eyes and said, "Hello, I'm Gogo. Do you want to be my friend?"

Lila was so happy. She hugged the goat and said, "Yes, I do. You are the best goat ever. Can I play with you?"

Gogo nodded and said, "Of course. Follow me. I'll show you around." He led her to the field, where they met other animals. They played with the cows, the sheep, the pigs, and the chickens. They had so much fun.

But then, Lila heard a loud noise. It was a wolf. The wolf was big and scary, with sharp teeth and claws. It growled and said, "I'm hungry. I want to eat a goat. And I see a tasty one right here." It pointed at Gogo.

Lila was scared. She wanted to protect Gogo, but she felt helpless. She was too small and weak to fight the wolf. She cried and said, "No, please, don't hurt Gogo. He is my friend. Go away, bad wolf."

Gogo was brave. He stood in front of Lila and said, "Don't worry, Lila. I'll save you. You are my friend, too. Go away, bad wolf. You can't have me or Lila."

The wolf laughed and said, "You can't stop me, little goat. I'm stronger and faster than you. I'll eat you both."

He jumped at Gogo, but Gogo dodged. He used his horns to hit the wolf. He kicked him with his hooves. He made loud noises to call for help. The other animals heard him and came to help. They chased the wolf away.

Lila was so relieved. She hugged Gogo and said, "Thank you, Gogo. You are my hero. You saved me and yourself. You are the best goat ever."

Gogo smiled and said, "You're welcome, Lila. You are my hero, too. You stayed with me and didn't run away. You are the best friend ever."

They hugged each other and said, "We are friends forever."

Lila woke up. She realized it was a dream. But it felt so real. She smiled and said, "I love you, Gogo. I hope I see you again in my dreams." She closed her eyes and fell asleep.

Suddenly, they heard a loud squawk and saw a big bird flying towards them. It was the mother bird and she was very angry. She saw Tom's hand near her eggs and thought he wanted to hurt them. She pecked at Tom's hand and made him cry.

"Ow, ow, ow! The bird bit me, Lily! Help me!" Tom shouted.

"Tom, I told you not to touch the eggs. You made the bird angry. Come on, let's go down," Lily said. She helped Tom climb down the tree. They ran to their mom who was sitting on a bench nearby.

"Mom, mom, a bird bit Tom. He touched her eggs and she got angry," Lily said.

"Oh, Tom, are you OK? Let me see your hand. It's just a scratch, don't worry. But you shouldn't touch the bird's eggs. They are not yours. They are her babies. How would you feel if someone touched your toys without asking?" Mom said.

"I'm sorry, Mom. I was curious. I won't touch the bird's eggs again. I learned my lesson," Tom said.

"That's good, Tom. I'm glad you learned your lesson. And I'm proud of you, Lily, for being careful and respectful. You are a good sister. Now, let's go home and have some ice cream," Mom said.

They hugged Mom and went home. They learned that they should not touch things that are not theirs and that they should respect other living things. They also learned that climbing trees can be fun but also dangerous. They had a good day and a good wake.

Lily and Ben were friends who liked to play with numbers. They had many number toys, like blocks, puzzles, and cards. They could count, add, and subtract very well. They also liked to be creative and make up their own number games.

One day, they decided to play a game called "Stomach Numbers". They took turns to eat some number snacks, like crackers, raisins, and cheese. Then they had to guess how many snacks were in their stomachs. They used their fingers to show their guesses.

Lily ate four crackers, six raisins, and two pieces of cheese. She guessed that she had twelve snacks in her stomach. She showed Ben her fingers. Ben ate three crackers, five raisins, and three pieces of cheese. He guessed that he had eleven snacks in his stomach. He showed Lily his fingers.

They both smiled and said, "We are good at Stomach Numbers!"

But soon, they started to feel sick. Their stomachs hurt and they felt like throwing up. They ran to the bathroom and cried. Their mom heard them and came to help. She asked them what happened.

"We played Stomach Numbers," Lily said. "We ate too many snacks and guessed how many were in our stomachs."

Mom shook her head and said, "That was not a good game. You should not eat too much or too fast. That can make your stomachs unhappy. You should eat only when you are hungry and stop when you are full. And you should eat healthy foods, like fruits and vegetables, not just snacks."

Lily and Ben nodded and said, "We are sorry, Mom. We learned our lesson. We will not play Stomach Numbers again. We will eat better and take care of our stomachs."

Mom hugged them and said, "I'm glad you understand. I love you both. Now, let me get you some water and some medicine to make you feel better."

Lily and Ben thanked Mom and drank the water and the medicine. They felt a little better and rested on the couch. They decided to play a different number game, one that did not involve eating. He jumped on the windowsill and grabbed the pie with his mouth. But he did not know that a girl was inside the house. The girl saw the fox and shouted. "Hey, fox! Give me back my pie! You cannot steal my pie!"

"Anna, listen to me," her mom said. "The forest is not like our home. There are many things that can hurt you or get you lost. You have to stay close to us and follow the path. Do you understand?"

"Yes, mom," Anna said. But she did not really listen. She thought the forest was fun and regular. She wanted to explore and play.

While her mom and dad were setting up the picnic, Anna saw a butterfly. She ran after it, leaving the path. She chased the butterfly until she came to a big tree. She saw a hole in the tree and wondered what was inside. She put her head in the hole and said hello.

"Hello, who are you?" a voice said. Anna was surprised. She saw a pair of big eyes and a long nose. It was a raccoon.

"I'm Anna," she said. "Who are you?"

"I'm Rocky," the raccoon said. "What are you doing in my home?"

"I'm sorry, I was just curious," Anna said. "I like your home. It's cozy and dark."

"Thank you, but you shouldn't be here," Rocky said. "The forest is not a regular place for you. There are many dangers and rules. You have to listen to your mom and dad. They know what's best for you."

Anna realized that Rocky was right. She had been foolish and rude. She apologized to Rocky and thanked him for his advice. She said goodbye and ran back to the path. She hoped her mom and dad were not worried.

She found them at the picnic spot. They were happy to see her, but also angry. They asked her where she had been and why she had not listened to them. Anna told them the truth. She said she had met a raccoon who had taught her a lesson. She said she was sorry and that she would listen to them from now on.

Her mom and dad hugged her and forgave her. They said they were proud of her for being honest and learning from her mistake. They said they loved her and wanted her to be safe and happy. They shared the picnic and enjoyed the forest together.

The moral of the story is: Listen to your parents, they know what's best for you. The forest is not a regular place, it has many dangers and rules. Be respectful of the animals and their homes. Be curious, but be careful.

One day, they went to the harbor with their mom and dad. The harbor was a big place with many boats and water and birds. Ben and Lily saw a big boat with a flag and a horn. They wanted to sing on the boat.

"Can we sing on the boat, mom?" Ben asked.

"Can we, can we, dad?" Lily asked.

Mom and dad looked at each other and smiled. "Sure, why not?" they said. "But you have to be careful and stay with us."

Ben and Lily were very happy. They ran to the boat and climbed on board. They saw many people and things on the boat. They saw a captain, a sailor, a fish, and a rope. They sang a song about the boat and the harbor.

"Boat, boat, you are so big and strong, you can go far and long, boat, boat, we like you a lot, you have a flag and a horn, boat, boat!"

"Harbor, harbor, you are so nice and blue, you have many boats and water and birds, harbor, harbor, we like you too, you have a dock and a light, harbor, harbor!"

They sang so loud and so fast that everyone on the boat heard them. Some people smiled and clapped. Some people frowned and shook their heads. Some people said, "What a crazy song! What a crazy pair!"

The captain heard them too. He did not like their song. He did not like their noise. He did not like their fun. He came to them and said, "Stop singing, you two! You are making too much noise! You are bothering me and everyone else! You are not welcome on my boat! Get off now!"

Ben and Lily were scared and sad. They did not understand why the captain was so mean. They did not want to stop singing. They did not want to get off the boat. They looked at their mom and dad for help.

Mom and dad were angry and sorry. They did not like how the captain treated their children. They did not think their children did anything wrong. They wanted to protect their children and their joy. They said to the captain, "How dare you, sir! Our children are just singing a harmless song! They are not making too much noise! They are not bothering anyone! They are welcome on your boat! We paid for our tickets! We will not get off!"

The captain and mom and dad argued for a long time. They raised their voices and pointed their fingers. They did not listen to each other. They did not care about each other. They made more noise than Ben and Lily ever did.

Ben and Lily felt bad and bored. They did not like to see their mom and dad fight. They did not like to see the captain yell. They did not like to be on the boat anymore. They wanted to go back to the harbor and sing somewhere else.

They held each other's hand and said, "Let's go, Ben. Let's go, Lily. We don't need this boat. We don't need this captain. We have each other. We have our song. We can sing anywhere we want."

They walked off the boat and back to the harbor. They found a nice spot by the water and the birds. They sang a new song about their love and their freedom.

"Lily, Lily, you are my sister and my friend, you make me brave and you make me sing, Lily, Lily, I love you so much, you have a hug and a voice, Lily, Lily!"

Lily and Ben smile. They hug each other. They are happy. They have learned a lesson. They have learned how to part and share.

The boy and the girl saw the acorn and the squirrel. They smiled. They thought the squirrel was cute and funny. They gave her the hat and took the acorn. They said "Thank you" and "Bye bye".

"See, Tom, the dog is nice. He likes us. Can we keep him?"

Tom shakes his head. "No, Sue, we can't. We have to find his owner. Maybe he has a collar with a name and a phone number."

One day, a boy named Tom saw a big bug on his bed. He hated bugs. He screamed and ran to his mom. "Mom, mom, there is a bug on my bed! It is scary and ugly and I hate it!"

His mom came to his room and looked at the bug. It was a harmless beetle. It had shiny wings and tiny legs. It did not bite or sting. "Tom, this is not a scary bug. It is a harmless bug. It is a beetle. It is a friend of the plants and the soil. It does not want to hurt you or your bed. It is just lost and looking for a home."

Tom did not believe his mom. He still hated the bug. He wanted to squash it with his shoe. He grabbed his shoe and ran to his bed. But his mom stopped him. "Tom, no! You cannot squash the bug. That is very mean and cruel. The bug has a life and a lung, just like you. It breathes and feels and thinks, just like you. How would you like it if someone squashed you with a shoe?"

Tom thought about what his mom said. He imagined how it would feel to be squashed by a shoe. He felt sorry for the bug. He did not want to hurt it. He put down his shoe and said, "I'm sorry, bug. I don't hate you anymore. You can stay on my bed. But please don't crawl on me. I don't like that."

The bug heard Tom and nodded. It crawled to the corner of the bed and stayed there. It was happy and grateful. Tom and his mom smiled and hugged. Tom learned to be kind and respectful to all living things, even bugs. He also learned that some things that look scary are not scary at all, but harmless and helpful. He was glad that his mom taught him that. He said, "Thank you, mom. You are the best. I love you."

The end.

"Wow, look at this!" Tom said. "It is so pretty!"

"Can I see it?" Lila asked.

Tom gave her the ring. She put it on her finger. It was too big for her, but she liked how it felt.

"A fairy?" Lila said. "Do you think there are fairies in the park?"

One day, Anna wanted to mix her dolls and Ben's cars. She thought it would be fun to make them ride together. She took some of Ben's cars and put them in her trunk. Then she took some of her dolls and put them in his box.

Ben did not like that. He wanted his cars to stay in his box. He did not want them to be with dolls. He said to Anna, "Stop! Give me back my cars! They are mine!"

Anna did not want to stop. She wanted to keep mixing. She said to Ben, "No! I like to mix! It is fun! You can play with my dolls!"

Ben was angry. He tried to take his cars from Anna's trunk. Anna was angry too. She tried to keep them in her trunk. They pulled and pushed and shouted at each other.

Anna and Ben stopped fighting. They looked at Mom. They felt sorry. They said to Mom, "We are sorry, Mom. We wanted to mix, but we did not agree. We made a mess."

Mom said to them, "It is okay to mix, but you have to ask first. And you have to respect each other's toys. You can mix some, but not all. And you have to clean up after you mix."

Anna and Ben nodded. They said to Mom, "Okay, Mom. We understand. We will ask and respect and clean up."

Mom smiled. She said to them, "Good. Now, why don't you mix some of your toys and make a story? You can use your imagination and have fun."

Anna and Ben smiled too. They said to Mom, "Okay, Mom. We will mix and make a story. Thank you, Mom."

They hugged Mom and then went back to their toys. They mixed some of their dolls and cars and made a story. They had fun and played nicely. They were not gloomy anymore. They were happy.
