"I wish we could go to the park," Anna said. "I want to swing and slide and run."

"Me too," Ben said. "But we can't. The park is wet and muddy."

They sighed and sat on the floor. They had no toys to play with. They had left them at the park yesterday.

"Maybe we can make a wish," Anna said. "Maybe the sun will come out and dry the park."

"How do we make a wish?" Ben asked.

Anna thought for a moment. She remembered what her mom had told her. "We need a star," she said. "A star can hear our wish and make it come true."

"But there are no stars now," Ben said. "It is day and the sky is dark."

Anna looked around the room. She saw a shiny sticker on the wall. It was shaped like a star. She had put it there last week.

"Look, Ben," she said. "There is a star. We can use that."

She ran to the wall and grabbed the sticker. She gave it to Ben. "You go first," she said. "Make a wish."

Ben closed his eyes and held the sticker. He wished very hard. He wished for the sun and the park and the fun.

He opened his eyes and gave the sticker to Anna. "Your turn," he said.

Anna closed her eyes and held the sticker. She wished very hard. She wished for the same thing as Ben.

She opened her eyes and smiled. She felt a warm breeze on her face. She heard a bird sing. She looked at the window and saw a bright light.

"Ben, look!" she said. "The sun is out. The rain is gone. The clouds are gone. The sky is blue."

"Let's go to the park," he said. "Let's go now."

"Can we go to the park, mom?" they asked. "Please, please, please."

"What's that noise?" Tom asked, as he stopped his car.

"Mom, mom, are you okay?" they shouted, as they ran to the kitchen.

They saw their mom holding the mixer, which was smoking and sparking. She looked scared and angry.

"Oh, no, the mixer is broken! It made a big mess!" she said, as she put the mixer on the counter.

She saw Tom and Lily, and smiled.

"Hi, kids, I'm sorry for the loud noise. I was trying to make a cake for you, but the mixer did not work. It made the cake increase and increase, until it was too big for the pan. Then it spilled over and burned. Look at the oven, it's full of cake!"

"Can we eat it?" Lily asked.

"No, sweetie, it's not good. It's burned and bitter. We have to throw it away. But don't worry, I have another cake mix. We can make a new cake, with a different mixer. Do you want to help me?" mom said.

"Yes, yes, we want to help!" Tom and Lily said.

"No, I don't like spicy food. It makes my mouth hurt. I like sweet food," Anna said. "My boat is going to France. They have yummy cakes and ice cream there. Do you like sweet food, Ben?"

"Yes, I like sweet food. But I also like spicy food. It makes me feel warm and strong. Can we share our food when we get to the ports?" Ben asked.

"OK, we can share. But you have to include some water too. Water helps when you eat spicy food. It makes your mouth feel better," Anna said.

"Deal. Water and food for both of us. And maybe some toys too. We can trade with the people at the ports. They might have different toys than us," Ben said.

They nodded and smiled. They continued to play with their boats, imagining all the different ports and foods and toys they would see and try. They had fun and learned new things. They were happy.

Lily and Tom are playing in the park. They like to swing, slide and run. Lily sees a big tree with many leaves. She wants to climb it and see the sky.

"Tom, look at that tree! Can we climb it?" Lily asks.

Tom shakes his head. "No, Lily, it is too high. You might fall and hurt yourself. Mommy said we have to be careful."

Lily does not listen. She runs to the tree and starts to climb. She feels happy and brave. She goes higher and higher. She sees the birds and the clouds.

"Look, Tom, I am so high!" Lily shouts.

Tom is scared. He sees Lily on the top of the tree. He wants her to come down.

"Lily, please come down! It is not safe! You might fall and hurt yourself!" Tom begs.

Lily does not listen. She wants to stay on the tree. She thinks it is fun. She reaches for a branch. But the branch is weak. It breaks. Lily falls.

"Help! Help!" Lily screams.

Tom runs to Lily. He sees her on the ground. She is crying. She has a cut on her knee. It is bleeding.

"Lily, are you okay? I am sorry you fell. You need medicine." Tom says.

He hugs Lily. He helps her stand up. He takes her to the bench. He finds a band-aid in his backpack. He puts it on Lily's knee.

"There, Lily, it will be better soon. The band-aid will stop the blood. The medicine will make the pain go away." Tom says.

Lily stops crying. She looks at Tom. She feels sorry.

"Thank you, Tom. You are a good brother. I am sorry I did not listen to you. I was silly. I will not climb the tree again." Lily says.

Tom smiles. He holds Lily's hand. He sees Mommy coming. She has a bottle of water and a cookie.

"Mommy, look, Lily fell from the tree. She has a band-aid and medicine. She is okay now." Tom says.

Mommy looks at Lily. She sees the band-aid and the cut. She feels worried.

"Oh, Lily, what happened? Are you hurt? Did you fall from the tree?" Mommy asks.

Lily nods. She tells Mommy what happened. She says she is sorry.

Mommy hugs Lily. She kisses her knee. She gives her some water and a cookie.

"It's okay, Lily. I am glad you are okay. You were brave. But you have to be careful. Trees are not for climbing. They are for looking and touching. Next time, listen to Tom. He loves you and wants you to be safe." Mommy says.

Lily nods. She eats the cookie. She feels better. She says she loves Mommy and Tom.

Mommy smiles. She says she loves Lily and Tom. She opens her arms. She hugs them both. They are happy. They are a family.

"Stop it, stop it!" Anna says. She is very angry. She pushes Ben away. She takes her paper and her paint. She runs to the other side of the room.

The cookie is not tasty anymore. It is soggy and mushy. It makes Ben sick.

"Yuck, yuck!" Ben says. He is very sick. He does not like the cookie. He does not like the water. He does not like anything.

He wishes Anna was nice to him. He wishes they could play with paint and make circles. He wishes they could be friends.

But Anna is not nice to him. She is not his friend. She is angry and mean.

They are both unhappy.

One day, he sees a man with a big camera. The man comes close to his cage and points the camera at him. Tom thinks the camera is a toy. He wants to have it. He reaches out his hand and grabs the camera. The man is angry and shouts at him.

Tom does not understand the man. He thinks the man is playing with him. He makes funny faces and noises at the man. He swings the camera around and hits the cage bars. The camera breaks into pieces. Tom is happy. He thinks he has improved his cage. He has a new toy to play with.

The man is very sad and mad. He runs away to find a zookeeper. He wants to get his camera back and make Tom pay for it. He does not know that Tom is just a curious and playful monkey. He does not know that Tom does not like his cage. He does not know that Tom is not stupid. He is just different.

But the spider moved. It ran towards Tom. Tom was surprised. He did not like the spider anymore. He wanted to run away too. But he could not. He was too scared. He felt like he could not move. He was frozen.

Lily heard Tom. She was hiding behind a tree. She felt sorry for Tom. She did not want him to be scared. She wanted to help him. She saw a big stick on the ground. It was heavy. She picked it up. She ran to Tom.

The boy looked surprised and said, "Really? You don't mind?" He took the ugly doll and looked at it. He said, "Maybe I can. Maybe it is not so funny. Maybe it is just different. Thank you for letting me play with it."

Lily smiled and said, "You're welcome. Maybe we can play together sometime. But you have to ask first, okay?"

The boy nodded and said, "Okay. I'm sorry for taking your doll. I won't do it again."

Lily said, "That's okay. I forgive you. What's your name?"

The boy said, "I'm Ben. What's yours?"

Lily said, "I'm Lily. And this is Anna."

Ben said, "Hi, Lily. Hi, Anna. Nice to meet you."

Lily said, "Nice to meet you too, Ben. Do you want to go on the slide with me?"

Ben said, "Sure. That sounds fun. Let's go."

They took their dolls and ran to the slide. They had fun sliding down and up again. They became friends.

"Let's run after it!" Sam said.

"OK!" Lily said.

They ran and ran, but the balloon was too fast. They crossed the street without looking. A car was coming. It honked loudly.

"Watch out!" a voice shouted.

Lily and Sam stopped. They saw a man in a white coat. He had wings and a halo. He was an angel.

"Are you OK?" the angel asked.

"Yes, thank you," Lily and Sam said.

The angel smiled. He said, "You are very lucky. I was here to save you. You should always be careful when you cross the street. You should always hold hands and look both ways. Do you understand?"

"Yes, we understand," Lily and Sam said.

The angel nodded. He said, "Good. Now, I have to go. But I have a gift for you. Here, take this balloon. It is a magic balloon. It will make you happy and kind."

He gave them the colorful balloon. It was warm and soft. Lily and Sam thanked him. They hugged him.

"Bye, angel," they said.

"Bye, children," the angel said. He flew away.

Lily and Sam looked at each other. They smiled. They held hands. They looked both ways. They crossed the street.

They went back to the park. They played with the balloon. They shared it with other children. They were happy and kind.

They said, "We want to be like the angel. We want to help others. We want to be friends forever."

They said, "When we grow up, we will marry each other. We will have a colorful wedding. We will invite the angel. He will be happy for us."

The end.

Tim and Mia painted the black star with their new colors. They made it look like a rainbow. The black star was now very pretty. They were happy with their work and showed it to their friends. All the kids loved the colorful star, and they all played together under the beautiful sky.

Joe said to Bob, "Why are you always so happy?" Bob said, "Why are you so grumpy?"
Joe replied, "I don't know. I just can't help it!"

Suddenly, Bob had an idea. He said, "Let's play a game! I will stand on one side of the rail, and you stand on the other side. Whenever I say something, you say the opposite. Maybe that will help you to be more happy!"

Joe agreed, so they played the game. Whenever Bob said, "I'm happy," Joe would say, "I'm grumpy." Bit by bit, Joe started to smile more and he didn't seem so grumpy any more.

By the end of the walk, Joe had a big smile on his face just like Bob! The two friends always made sure to never forget their special game and continued to play it whenever they went for a walk.

Suddenly, Emma had an idea. She quickly ran inside, grabbed a small bucket and ran outside again. She began to fill the bucket with small pebbles and rocks. She knew what she had to do. She took a deep breath and walked to the edge of her yard, the bucket in her little hands.

She slowly threw pebble after pebble into the air, dreaming that one of them would spark a rain cloud. But still, nothing happened.

With a heavy heart, Emma returned to the house. She was so disappointed but she had tried her best to fix the dryness. No matter what, at least she had tried.

Joe was walking in the park with his mum. He was so alert, looking out for bugs, birds and squirrels. All of a sudden, a loud noise shook the park! Joe looked around and saw two people doing yoga. Joe was fascinated and he clapped with excitement.

But the people weren't happy. One of them started to snap at Joe! He was shouting, and Joe was scared. His mum came over to help, but it was too late. Joe started to cry and ran away.

The people stopped practising their yoga and watched Joe go. The snap had scared him and he ran away, never to be seen again. Joe hadn't expected to be treated so badly, but that was the bad ending to his story.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy called Tom. Tom was very impatient, he wanted to go upstairs and play. Everyday, his mommy and daddy say 'not yet'. 

One day, when Tom was three, his mommy and daddy said 'finally, you can go upstairs!'. Tom was very excited and he ran upstairs as fast as he could. 

When Tom reached the top of the stairs, he saw something funny. It was a big brown bear! Tom cried "Wow!" and the bear said "Hullo!" Tom was amazed and he said: "Are you real?". The big brown bear said "Yes, I am real - let's play together!" 

Tom was so happy! He and the bear played together for hours and hours. Tom was having so much fun, he did not want to stop. 

Finally, it was time for Tom to go home. He said goodbye to the big brown bear, hugged him, and then ran all the way down the stairs. All the way home, Tom was happy to have met a real bear.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Candace who had a very special pet. It was a puppy named Spot who she loved very much. One day, Spot went out for a walk and didn't come back.

Candace was very sad, but she was determined to rescue Spot. She searched all around her neighborhood, but she couldn't find him. Finally, she heard a little yelp and realised that Spot was stuck in a bush!

Candace quickly dug him out and was so relieved to see him safe and sound. When she noticed that Spot had a little cut on his paw, she was very scared of what might have happened. She decided to take him to the vet to get it fixed and Spot was brave during the visit.

The vet said that Spot was fine and he gave Candace some medicine to help the cut heal. Candace was so proud of Spot for being brave and she was so glad that she was able to rescue him! She gave him an extra special hug and Spot was happy to be home with his best friend.

Once upon a time there was a princess who lived in a cool castle. Every day the princess would put on her crown and go on a walk. One day she decided to guess what it must be like to live outside the castle. So she packed some clothes, her crown, and left the castle.

She soon found herself in a strange land and she quickly realised that it wasn't as cool as it had looked from the castle. She spoke to people and listened to their stories. At the end of the day, she realised that while it's nice to explore different places, it's important to be happy with the place you already have.

The princess was so happy with her lesson that she decided it was time to go back to the castle. She was welcomed home with hugs and smiles. The princess was glad that she went on her journey, but she also knew that life was cool in her castle.

The moral of this story is that life is cool where ever you are - as long as you are happy where you are. So it's ok to guess what it might be like in different places, but it's just as important to be happy with the place you are in.

Once upon a time, there was a magical blanket. The blanket was very impressive. It could melt anything it touched.

One day, there was a little girl named Sarah. She was only three years old, but she loved her blanket. But one day, it started to snow and Sarah was very cold.

Then, Sarah remembered her special blanket. She grabbed her blanket and hugged it tight. Suddenly, the snow around her started to melt! Thanks to the magical blanket, she stayed warm and happy.

The blanket was so magical and impressive. Sarah hugged it tight and thanked it for its warmth. From that day on, she stayed warm and happy whenever she had her blanket with her.

Once there was a little girl called Lucy. She was very unhappy, because she wanted to learn to play the piano. Every day, she would look out the window at the beautiful piano in the park. She tried to be brave and asked her mom if she could have her own piano. But her mom said no.

One night, Lucy went out in the park and saw the piano again. She decided to throw a stone at the piano and break it. Lucy felt so angry and frustrated! She wished she could just play the piano. But then something amazing happened.

When the stone hit the piano, it started to play a beautiful song. Lucy was so amazed that she just stood there and listened. Suddenly, Lucy realized that she should find other ways to express her feelings instead of being angry. 

From then on, Lucy stopped throwing stones and started to find other healthy ways to express her emotions.

The moral of the story is that even when we get angry, it is important to find other outlets for our emotions rather than using violence.

John had hurt his mouth. It was a big cut, and it hurt. He cried and cried, feeling guilty for jumping too high during his game. His mum saw him, and hugged him tight. She kissed his forehead and said softly "It's ok, I will help you heal". She then washed the cut, and put a bandage on it.

John sighed in relief. He felt better. His mum smiled at him and said "See, your mouth is all healed now!" John smiled back and said "Thanks, Mum!" Everything was ok again.

John now knew he had to be careful when playing. He didn't want to feel guilty again! He hugged his mum, happy that she had helped him heal his hurt mouth.

Once upon a time there was an artist who loved to paint. Every day the artist would go to the park and paint pictures of the beautiful flowers and trees. One day the artist saw something magical in the park; a deep network of silver shimmering stars in the night sky. The artist was so amazed by the beauty of this network that they decided to paint it. 

The artist worked day and night to try and capture the beauty of this deep network in the painting. However, no matter how much the artist painted, they just couldn't capture the sparkles of the stars. The artist was getting frustrated and so they tried and tried and tried, but they just couldn't get it just right. 

Eventually the artist was so angry that they ripped up the painting in fury. The stars of the deep network were never seen again in the park. The artist was sad and realised that it was all their fault. The painting was destroyed, and the artist never painted again.

Once upon a time, there was a girl who lived in a big town. In the town, she loved to get pastries. Every day she would get a pastry, but she never got healthy pastries.

One day, the girl's mom said she would only get one pastry a week, and it had to be a healthy one. The girl got very upset about this and decided to get a pastry every day anyway.

For a while, the girl was able to get pastries every day, but then one day she got caught. Her mom was very angry and said she could no longer get pastries. The girl was very sad, but she knew it was her own fault.

The girl learned her lesson and from then on, she only got healthy pastries once a week.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy who loved to explore. One day, he was careful to shut the door when he went out to play. He walked all around his neighbourhood and looked for interesting things. But he couldn't find any. 

The little boy was feeling a bit sad, so he sat down on a bench in the park. He looked around and noticed a beautiful flower in one of the flowerbeds. He knew it was special and wanted to take it home with him. 

But there was something stopping him. He felt like his heart was telling him to be careful. So he took one careful step back and decided to leave the flower in the park. 

The little boy was happy with his decision. He looked back at the flower and smiled before he went back home. As he shut the door, he felt proud of himself for being so careful.
